title:
Consultation paper (16 pages) on policy options to regulate e-bike safety and survey (18 pages).

You can access the consultation paper and survey on the ACCC’s Consultation Hub.
description:
The ACCC is consulting on options for a mandatory safety standard for electrically power-assisted cycles, commonly known as e-bikes and associated devices, including conversion kits and tampering devices, and e-bike batteries and chargers.

E-bikes are bicycles fitted with electric motors to provide power-assistance to riders and are intended to be primarily powered by peddling. E-bike conversion kits consist of a motor, battery and other components that convert conventional pedal bicycles into e-bikes. Tampering devices are products that allow modification to an e-bikes power output and speed.

The popularity of e-bikes has grown significantly in recent years, and these devices provide many community benefits. However, fires, injuries and deaths related to e-bikes have also increased and is of significant concern.

We are consulting on options for a mandatory safety standard to address the risks posed by e-bikes and associated devices, while maintaining the benefits e-bikes provide.

A mandatory safety standard could apply minimum safety requirements or restrictions to the supply of e-bikes and associated devices.

This consultation seeks views on the introduction of a mandatory safety standard for e‑bikes, including the scope and application.

objectivesFreeText:
The policy objectives are to:

  • Reduce injury and death resulting from the supply of unsafe e-bikes and associated devices, and reduce associated cost of injury.
  • Maintain community benefits from e-bikes and conversion kits by ensuring those that are supplied are safe.
  • Ensure competition and trade are not significantly impacted by regulatory intervention.

title:
Draft Unsafe Goods (Consumer Sand Products) Notice 2026 (6 pages, in English), https://www.mbie.govt.nz/have-your-say/consultation-on-draft-unsafe-goods-consumer-sand-products-notice-2026.

The final notice has been issued by the Minister of Commerce and Consumer Affairs under section 31 of the Fair Trading Act 1986. The notice declares certain toys containing sand and decorative, craft or artistic goods containing accessible sand to be unsafe goods unless prescribed asbestos testing requirements have been met. The notice incorporates by reference:

  • ISO 22262-2:2026, Air quality — Bulk materials — Part 2: Quantitative determination of asbestos by gravimetric and microscopical methods (50 pages, in English);
  • ISO 22262-2:2014, Air quality — Bulk materials — Part 2: Quantitative determination of asbestos by gravimetric and microscopical methods (47 pages, in English);
  • ISO 22262-1:2012 Air quality — Bulk materials — Part 1: Sampling and qualitative determination of asbestos in commercial bulk materials (70 pages, in English.
description: Since November 2025, New Zealand suppliers have undertaken 23 recalls of consumer sand products following the detection of asbestos contamination, affecting approximately 46,000 units. Research has demonstrated that asbestos fibres may become airborne during normal use of some sand products, creating a risk of inhalation and associated adverse health effects. The proposed measure seeks to prevent the supply of asbestos-contaminated consumer sand products in New Zealand. The use of an internationally recognised testing method and laboratory accreditation requirements intend to provide a consistent and reliable basis for demonstrating compliance. The measure is intended as an interim requirement pending development of longer-term product safety regulation addressing asbestos contamination in consumer sand products (hence the urgency).

description:
To reduce GHG emissions from the use of Hydrofluorocarbons (HFC) refrigerants in the Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning (RAC) sector, NEA will introduce limits on the Global Warming Potential (GWP) of refrigerants to restrict the import and supply of equipment using refrigerants with high GWP. 

 

Since 2022, NEA has imposed GWP limits for household air-conditioners, refrigerators and water-cooled chillers used for large building cooling systems.

 

The Environmental Protection and Management (Prescribed Regulated Goods) Order 2022 and Environmental Protection and Management (Regulated Goods and Registered Suppliers) Regulation 2022 will be amended to:

  1. Introduce GWP limit of 150 for refrigerants used in centralised commercial refrigeration systems, with effect from 1 July 2027.
  2. Introduce GWP limit of 150 for refrigerants used in passenger cabin air-conditioning systems in Motor Vehicles (i.e. passenger cars/taxis and light goods vehicles), with effect from 1 July 2028.
     

The GWP limits apply only to newly supplied equipment. 

 

Details of the restrictions are available on NEA’s website at: https://www.nea.gov.sg/our-services/climate-change-energy-efficiency/climate-change/reducing-ghg-emissions-from-the-use-of-refrigerants-in-rac-sector

title: Voluntary Consensus Standards Update; Formaldehyde Emission Standards for Composite Wood Products
description:
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is publishing a final rule to update the incorporation by reference of several voluntary consensus standards in the Agency's formaldehyde standards for composite wood products regulations under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) due to the standards having been updated or superseded by the issuing organizations. These new standards primarily update test methods and product standards concerning composite wood products that use formaldehyde. EPA is also conforming these updated standards in the scope and definitional sections in the final rule and incorporating by reference a new small scale quality control chamber test method, similar to current methods already incorporated by reference. EPA is also removing one standard that was previously incorporated by reference to avoid redundancy, given that another identical, internationally recognized version of the standard is already incorporated by reference in this rule.

 

This final rule is effective on 27 November 2026. The incorporation by reference of certain material listed in the rule is approved by the Director of the Federal Register as of 27 November 2026. The incorporation by reference of certain other material listed in the rule was approved by the Director of the Federal Register as of 10 February 2017, 7 February 2018, 21 August 2019, and 23 March 2023.

title: Additional Reconsideration Standards of Performance for New, Reconstructed, and Modified Sources and Emissions Guidelines for Existing Sources: Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review
description:
Proposed rule - The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing amendments to the New Source Performance Standards and Emission Guidelines for the Crude Oil and Natural Gas Source Category to address additional concerns raised with prior regulatory amendments finalized in March 2024. Specifically, the EPA is proposing changes in response to certain petitions for reconsideration of the March 2024 amendments, changes based on policy decisions and supporting legal interpretations, and changes that correct and clarify the regulatory text of the new source performance standards and emission guidelines. First, the EPA proposes to rescind the Super Emitter Program. Second, the EPA proposes to subcategorize different types of well sites affected and designated facilities to address issues related to the requirements finalized in March 2024 for marginal well sites and conventional well sites. Third, the EPA proposes changes to address issues related to liquids unloading, process controllers, pumps, fugitive emissions, storage vessels, covers and closed vent systems, equipment leaks at gas plants, and associated gas. Fourth, the EPA proposes changes to certain requirements finalized in March 2024 related to control devices and to provide owners and operators the option to conduct optical gas imaging surveys according to Appendix K for gas processing facilities. Lastly, the EPA proposes changes to correct inadvertent errors and to clarify regulatory language.

 

EPA will hold a virtual public hearing starting at 10am Eastern Time on 16 November 2026 for the Proposed Reconsideration of the 2024 Final Clean Air Act Rule. Pre-registration is now open. If you would like to provide testimony at the public hearing, please register at https://survey.alchemer.com/s3/9078544/OG-Recon2-PublicHearing-2026.  For any questions or concerns, please contact the public hearing team at OG-Recon2-PublicHearing-2026@rti.org.

title: Draft Decree amending and supplementing a number of articles of Government Decree No. 163/2025/ND-CP dated 29 June 2025 detailing a number of articles and prescribing measures for organizing and guiding the implementation of the Law on Pharmacy
description:
The draft Decree contains the following provisions:
6.1. Amendments to reduce and simplify administrative procedures:
- Implementation of the plan to reduce and simplify administrative procedures relating to production and business activities under Resolution No. 66.16/2026/NQ-CP.
- Implementation of the plan to reduce and simplify administrative procedures based on data under Resolution No. 66.7/NQ-CP.
6.2. Guidance on the amendments and additions to the Law on Pharmacy proposed in the draft Law amending and supplementing a number of articles of the Law on Children, the Law on Persons with Disabilities, the Law on Medical Examination and Treatment, the Law on Pharmacy, the Law on the Elderly and the Law on Health Insurance, to align the entry into force of the Decree with that of the amending Law:
- Implementation of the plan to decentralize the administrative procedure for issuing Certificates of Confirmation of Drug Advertising Content by authorizing provincial-level People's Committees to process applications and issue these certificates, which would be valid nationwide.
- Amendments and additions to provisions on the publication and republication of proposed wholesale drug prices in Articles 114, 119 and 130, and addition of Article 115a on the procedures for receiving submissions for such publication and republication; provisions specifying which drugs may have their proposed wholesale prices published after the first batch has been sold on the market; procedures for submitting recommendations concerning published or republished proposed wholesale drug prices; and responsibilities for sharing data on drugs, medicinal raw materials cleared through customs for export or import, including drug import prices, for regulatory purposes.
6.3. Provisions to address practical issues requiring immediate resolution during the implementation of Decree No. 163/2025/ND-CP:
- Amendments and additions to Article 21 to provide for publication of information on the list of pharmacies in a pharmacy chain after the establishment organizing the pharmacy chain has been granted a Certificate of Eligibility for Pharmaceutical Business.
- Amendment and supplementation of the title of Article 70 by adding the phrase “semi-finished drugs for export”.
- Amendments and additions to Articles 78 and 82 to cover drugs for State health program where the drug provider has been designated in a decision of the Minister of Health approving the contractor selection arrangements for a procurement package involving purchases through international organizations under the special-case contractor selection procedure prescribed by the law on bidding; establishments conducting pharmaceutical activities for non-commercial purposes would also be authorized to import such drugs.
- Amendments and additions to Article 85 to cover internal transfers within medical examination and treatment establishments.
- Amendments and additions to Article 96 to allow a Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) inspection report from the competent inspecting authority to be replaced by a GMP inspection report from a Stringent Regulatory Authority (SRA), or a pharmaceutical regulatory authority recognized by the Ministry of Health on the basis of the World Health Organization (WHO) classification, or a report of a GMP inspection conducted by WHO under its Prequalification Program; the requirement to submit an “updated Site Master File” would be waived for foreign manufacturing establishments assessed on the basis of recognition or mutual recognition under Article 94. The amendment would also clarify the responsibilities of registration applicants and manufacturing establishments, as well as establishments that look up the documents specified in Clause 5 of Article 96 and use the information obtained from them.
- Amendments and additions concerning format and presentation to ensure clarity and transparency and prevent differing interpretations of legal provisions.
- Amendments and additions to certain forms in the Appendices to Decree No. 163/2025/ND-CP to align them with the amendments and additions in the draft Decree.

title: Proposal P1067 – Health Star Rating System: 2nd Call for Submissions and Supporting Documents.
description:
FSANZ has prepared a proposed draft amendment to the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code (the Code) to mandate the display of a Health Star Rating (HSR) symbol on food for sale in Australia and New Zealand. The 2nd call for submissions provides FSANZ’s assessment and the proposed draft amendment, which would require the HSR to be calculated using a prescribed algorithm and the HSR symbol to be displayed on the front of most packaged foods for retail sale that are required to bear a nutrition information panel, subject to specified exemptions and prohibitions.  

FSANZ seeks submissions on the proposed regulatory approach to inform its final assessment and a decision on whether to approve, amend or reject the proposed draft amendment.
productsFreeText: Imported and domestically produced packaged foods for retail sale in Australia and New Zealand that are required to bear a label, subject to certain exemptions and prohibitions.
objectivesFreeText:
Diet plays an important role in overall health and wellbeing. Poor diet can contribute to overweight and obesity and increase the risk of diet-related non-communicable diseases. Around two-thirds of the Australian and New Zealand population are currently overweight or obese, and an estimated 15% of deaths in Australasia are attributable to dietary risks. National dietary guidelines emphasise the importance of choosing a variety of nutritious foods and limiting foods high in saturated fat, sugars and sodium.

 

The Health Star Rating (HSR) system is a front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPL) scheme that summarises a food’s overall nutritional profile using a simple star rating. Evidence indicates tools such as FoPL, used alongside other broader public health strategies, can improve consumer understanding of the healthfulness of foods and support healthier choices, with interpretive summary indicators like the HSR system generally performing favourably compared to other FoPL systems.

 

The objective of the HSR system is to provide a quick, easy, standardised way for consumers to compare the nutritional value of similar foods to help them make informed healthier food choices in-line with dietary guidelines.

 

Most consumers agree the HSR symbol makes it easier to identify healthier foods, and a majority report using the system at least sometimes when shopping. However, even though the system has been implemented on a voluntary basis for over 10 years, low uptake and selective use of the system by industry have limited effective consumer use.

 

The objective of this proposal is to consider requiring the HSR symbol on foods for sale in Australia and New Zealand to better support healthier food choices and thereby contribute to broader public health efforts to reduce the prevalence of overweight, obesity and diet-related non-communicable diseases in Australia and New Zealand.

title: Draft Decree amending and supplementing a number of articles of the Decrees in the field of manufacturing, assembling and importing road motor vehicles and the Decree detailing a number of articles of the Railway Law, amending and supplementing: Decree No. 116/2017/NĐ-CP on conditions for manufacturing, assembling, importing and warranty and maintenance service business of automobiles; Decree No. 60/2023/NĐ-CP on inspection and certification of quality, technical safety and environmental protection of imported automobiles and imported components under international treaties to which Vietnam is a party; and Decree No. 16/2026/NĐ-CP detailing a number of articles of the Railway Law
description:
The draft Decree amends and supplements a number of articles of Decree No. 116/2017/NĐ-CP dated 17 October 2017 (as amended and supplemented by Decrees No. 17/2020/NĐ-CP, No. 14/2026/NĐ-CP and No. 117/2026/NĐ-CP), Decree No. 60/2023/NĐ-CP dated 16 August 2023 (as amended and supplemented by Decree No. 14/2026/NĐ-CP), and Decree No. 16/2026/NĐ-CP dated 14 January 2026 of the Government.
The draft Decree applies to enterprises manufacturing, assembling and importing automobiles in Vietnam, as well as relevant agencies, organizations and individuals. 
Its main contents are as follows:
1. Amendments and supplements to Decree No. 116/2017/NĐ-CP (Chapter I)
The draft Decree provides amendments and supplements to the government’s Decree no. 116/2017/ND-CP stipulating conditions for the manufacture, assembly, and import of automobiles, and the provision of automobile warranty and maintenance services (as amended and supplemented by Decree no. 17/2020/ND-CP dated February 5, 2020; Decree no. 14/2026/ND-CP dated January 13, 2026; and Decree no. 117/2026/ND-CP dated April 3, 2026) (referred to as Decree no. 116/2017/ND-CP, which stipulates the conditions for automobile manufacturing, assembly and importation, removing the business of automobile warranty and maintenance services from its scope of regulation.
2. Amendments and supplements to Decree No. 60/2023/NĐ-CP on the inspection and certification of imported automobiles (Chapter II)
The draft Decree provides amendments and supplements to the government’s Decree no. 60/2023/ND-CP dated august 16, 2023, regarding the inspection and certification of technical safety quality and environmental protection for imported automobiles and components in accordance with international treaties to which Viet Nam is a party (as amended and supplemented by the government’s Decree no. 14/2026/ND-CP) 
In the draft Decree, Appendix VI attached to Decree No. 60/2023/NĐ-CP shall be replaced by Appendix I attached to the draft Decree.
3. Amendments and supplements to Decree No. 16/2026/NĐ-CP detailing a number of articles of the Railway Law (Chapter III)
In the draft Decree, Clause 1 of Article 26 and Clause 1 of Article 35 are repealed.

title: Draft MOPH Notification (No. …) B.E. ...., issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 Re: “Flavoured Milk” (No.3) ;
description:
This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. .... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: "Flavoured Milk " (No. 3) amends the labelling requirements for name designations of flavoured milk.

The main objective is to revise and clarify the food name designations on the label for flavoured milk produced from milk powder or other milk components (such as whey, casein, lactose, or other recombined milk solids). The label must explicitly declare statements indicating the use of milk powder or recombined milk components as part of the food name (e.g., "obtained from milk powder" or "obtained from recombining separated components of cow's milk"). This amendment aims to ensure that consumers receive accurate and transparent information on product labels and to enhance consumer protection.

title: Draft MOPH Notification (No. …) B.E. ...., issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: “Cow’s Milk” (No.3)
description:
This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. .... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 Re: "Cow’s Milk " (No. 3) amends the definitions of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk", as well as the name designations of these food products.

a. Amend the definition of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" to clarify that it is drawn exclusively from the cow, and include additional processing methods to comprehensively cover current practices, such as sterilization and UHT.

b. Amend the definition of "recombined milk" to explicitly state that it is produced from milk powder or by recombining separated cow’s milk components, such as whey, casein, and lactose, and add requirements specifying that the quality or standards of recombined milk shall be equivalent to those of fresh plain fluid cow's milk or plain fluid cow's milk.

title: Law of Ukraine  of 13 October 2026 No. 5013 “On Amendments to the Tax Code of Ukraine and Certain Other Laws of Ukraine Regarding the Postponement of the Introduction of Electronic Traceability of the Circulation of Alcoholic Beverages, Tobacco Products and Liquids Used in Electronic Cigarettes”
description:
The Law amends the Tax Code of Ukraine and certain other laws to postpone the introduction of the electronic traceability system of the circulation of alcoholic beverages, tobacco products and liquids used in electronic cigarettes.

The Law postpones the introduction of the electronic excise stamp system from 1 November 2026 to 1 July 2027. It provides for the electronic traceability system to operate in test mode until 30 June 2027 and in full operation from 1 July 2027.

The Law establishes transitional arrangements for the registration of economic operators in the electronic system, the circulation of products bearing paper excise stamps and the application of financial penalties during the transition period. It sets specific deadlines for the registration of economic operators, including 1 April 2027 for operators holding the relevant licences as of 1 January 2027.

The Law also provides that alcoholic beverages, tobacco products and liquids used in electronic cigarettes manufactured in Ukraine or imported into Ukraine before 1 July 2027 and bearing paper excise stamps may remain in circulation until 31 December 2028, inclusive. Their circulation is governed by the legislation applicable before 1 July 2027 concerning products bearing paper excise stamps, without applying the requirements of the Tax Code of Ukraine and the relevant Law concerning the operation of the electronic system.

Alcoholic beverages, tobacco products and liquids used in electronic cigarettes imported into Ukraine from 1 July 2027 are to be marked with graphic elements of electronic excise stamps in accordance with the procedure established by law.

title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Extension of Collection; Comment Request; Standard for the Flammability of Mattresses and Mattress Pads and Standard for the Flammability (Open Flame) of Mattress Sets
description:
As required by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC or Commission) announces that the Commission has submitted to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) a request for extension of approval of information collection requirements associated with the Standard for the Flammability of Mattresses and Mattress Pads and the Standard for the Flammability (Open Flame) of Mattress Sets. OMB previously approved the collection of information under control number 3041-0014. OMB's most recent extension of approval will expire on 31 October 2026. On 18 June 2026, CPSC published a notice in the Federal Register (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/590/Rev.1/Add.4) to announce the agency's intention to seek extension of approval of the collection of information. The Commission received four public comments. By publication of this notice, the Commission announces that CPSC has submitted to OMB a request for extension of approval of that collection of information.

 

Submit comments on the collection of information by 27 November 2026.

title: Draft Commission Implementing Regulation concerning the non-renewal of the approval of the active substance phenmedipham in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council, and amending Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 540/2011
description:
This draft Commission Implementing Regulation provides that the approval of the active substance phenmedipham is not renewed in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009. Member States shall withdraw authorisations for plant protection products containing phenmedipham as an active substance. The non-renewal of approval is based on the first evaluation of the substance for use as a pesticide active substance in the EU under Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009. The substance was formerly assessed and approved under Directive 91/414/ EEC.

This decision only concerns the placing on the market of this substance and plant protection products containing it. Following non-approval and the expiry of all grace periods for stocks of products containing this substance, separate action will be taken on MRLs and a separate notification will be made in accordance with SPS procedures.

objectives.name: Protection of human health or safety (TBT)
Protection of animal or plant life or health (TBT)

objectivesFreeText:
In order for an active substance to be approved in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 (concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market), it must be demonstrated that the substance is not harmful to human health, animal health or the environment. Criteria are listed in Article 4 of the Regulation (and also detailed in Annex II thereto) which must be met to enable approval. 

During the evaluation and peer-review of phenmedipham, two critical areas of concerns and several areas that could not be finalised were identified. These are detailed in the conclusion of the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA): phenmedipham meets the criteria to be identified as an endocrine disruptor for the T-modality for non-target organisms other than mammals and effects at population level cannot be excluded and the technical specifications proposed by both applicants are not covered by the batches used in the key toxicological studies. In addition, several parts of the risk assessment could not be finalised by EFSA, including the consumer risk assessment via dietary intake and the risk assessment to aquatic organisms (algae). The outcome of the risk assessment, as documented in the EFSA Conclusion, identifies twenty-one data gaps. Although the applicant, when commenting on the EFSA Conclusion, indicated that thirteen of the twenty-one data gaps could be solved in applications for the renewal of product authorisations at Member State level, this is not possible because at least one safe use must be identified at the approval level (as confirmed by the ECJ in its recent judgement in case C-316/24 P on cypermethrin). 

These concerns mean that phenmedipham does not meet the approval criteria as outlined in Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 and therefore, the approval of phenmedipham should not be renewed for the use in plant protection products.

Existing authorisations will need to be withdrawn; Member States must withdraw existing plant protection products containing phenmedipham at the latest by 6 months from the date of entry into force. A period of grace in line with Article 46 of Regulation 1107/2009 is allowed for and shall expire at the latest 12 months from the entry into force (allowing for a final season of use).

title: Wireless Telecommunications Bureau Announces Upper C-Band Clearinghouse Selection Criteria and Submission Process
description:
In this document, the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau (Bureau) announces that it has received detailed selection criteria and related submission instructions for proposals for the position of Upper C-band Clearinghouse. In Upper C-band (3.98-4.2 GHz); Expanding Flexible Use of the 3.7 to 4.2 GHz Band, GN Docket Nos. 25-59 and 18- 122, Report and Order, Order of Proposed Modification, and Order on Reconsideration, FCC 26-46 (24 July 2026) (Upper C-band R&O), the Commission provided for the creation of an independent, third-party Upper C-band Clearinghouse to oversee the cost-related aspects of the Upper C-band transition, including the receipt, review, and disposition of all actual cost and lump sum reimbursement claims. The Upper C-band Clearinghouse will also administer the rebates for adjacent band radio altimeter retrofits.

 

Potential clearinghouse candidates must email the selection committee with any questions about the selection criteria or submission requirements no later than 23 October 2026. Potential clearinghouse candidates must submit proposals according to the filing instructions contained in the selection committee's notification no later than 9 November 2026.

title: Regulatory Guide: Acceptability of ASME OM-2 Code, Component Testing Requirements at Nuclear Facilities
description:
The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is confirming the effective date of 18 August 2026, for Revision 0 of Regulatory Guide (RG) 1.220, ''Acceptability of ASME OM-2 Code, Component Testing Requirements at Nuclear Facilities.'' The RG was noticed in the Federal Register on 4 June 2026 (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/2288), with a follow up Correction to the Notice, published on 22 June 2026 (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/2288/Corr.1), stating the effective date of 18 August 2026. This new RG endorses, with a regulatory position, the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Operation and Maintenance OM-2 Code, Component Testing Requirements at Nuclear Facilities, 2024 Edition, and describes an approach that is acceptable to the NRC staff for the development and implementation of an Inservice Testing (IST) Program for all types of nuclear facilities.

 

The effective date of 18 August 2026, for the direct final RG 1.220, Revision 0, published on 4 June 2026 (91 FR 33770), as corrected on 22 June 2026 (91 FR 37152), is confirmed.

title: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards; Modernization of FMVSS No. 108 To Accommodate ADS-Equipped Vehicles
description: Notice of proposed rulemaking - The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is proposing to amend Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 108, ''Lamps, reflective devices, and associated equipment.'' The proposed updates to the standard are intended to remove unnecessary requirements and to provide design flexibility without impact on vehicle safety. The first two proposed changes would amend the test voltage specification for integral beam type headlamps and remove requirements that apply to vertical headlamp arrangements. Further proposed changes address vehicles equipped with Automated Driving Systems (ADS) that do not have manually operated driving controls. Those modifications would limit the application of certain requirements for manually operated turn signal, hazard warning signal, and beam switching controls to vehicles with manually operated driving controls. The changes are intended to address regulatory burdens and costs associated with equipment that does not fulfill the same purpose or provide safety benefits in an ADS-equipped vehicle without manually operated driving controls as in a vehicle with such controls. The changes would also narrow certain requirements for telltales to vehicles with manually operated driving controls and incorporate the term ''telltale'' where appropriate throughout the standard. Finally, a proposed addition to the standard would allow cyan-colored ADS marker lamps as optional motor vehicle lighting equipment in ADS-equipped vehicles.

title: Amendment 09:2026 QCVN 09:2015/BCT National technical regulation for towel paper and toilet tissue paper (Annex Decree)
description:
Viet Nam informs WTO Members that the Ministry of Industry and Trade adopted Circular No. 62/2026/TT-BCT dated 30 September 2026 promulgating Amendment 09:2026 QCVN 09:2015/BCT National technical regulation for towel paper and toilet tissue paper. The Circular will enter into force on 15 November 2026.

The draft measure was previously notified in G/TBT/N/VNM/429 Amendment 09:2026 QCVN 09:2015/BCT National technical regulation for towel paper and toilet tissue paper.

This addendum notifies the adoption and availability of the final text. The adoption date above replaces the proposed adoption dates in the previous notifications.

 

Scope & Definitions: Clarifies the definition of tissue paper (including large-roll tissue paper intended for further processing).

 

Technical Requirements & Chemicals: Updates requirements for chemical management during production, mandating compliance with the Law on Chemicals No. 69/2025/QH15.

 

Product Labeling: Labeling must be carried out in accordance with Decree No. 37/2026/NĐ-CP, which provides guidelines for the Law on Product and Goods Quality.

 

Conformity Assessment & Certification:

- Declaration of conformity must follow either Method 5 or Method 7, as stipulated in Circular 14/2026/TT-BKHCN.

- A certificate of conformity issued under Method 5 shall be valid for no more than 3 years.

- Assessments are based on certification results from an accredited certification body, or on self-assessment results derived from testing conducted by an accredited/designated laboratory.

Update of Testing Standards (Test Methods): Incorporates and references the latest equivalent international standards (ISO/EN) for physical and mechanical properties.The notified final documents are Circular No. 62/2026/TT-BCT (2 pages) and Amendment 01:2026 QCVN 09:2015/BCT (7 pages), in Vietnamese. The complete final text is attached and is available at the link provided above.

 

Responsible agency: Ministry of Industry and Trade.

 

Technical contact: Viet Nam Industry Agency, 54 Hai Ba Trung Street, Cua Nam Ward, Ha Noi, Viet Nam. Mr Duong Xuan Dieu; telephone: +84 912 215 854; email: dieudx@moit.gov.vn.

 

National enquiry point: Viet Nam TBT Enquiry Point, Commission for Standards, Metrology and Quality of Viet Nam, 8 Hoang Quoc Viet Street, Nghia Do Ward, Ha Noi, Viet Nam. Email: tbtvn@mst.gov.vn.

Comply with the provisions of Law No. 78/2025/QH15; to modernise conformity assessment requirements towards risk-based management in line with Decree No. 37/2026/ND-CP and Decree No. 22/2026/ND-CP; to ensure consistency, uniformity, and conformity with the current legal system.

title: Draft Commission Implementing Regulation laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards access to and use of certain information in the battery passport
description: This draft Commission Implementing Regulation concerns the parts of the EU battery passport for which access is not public, but restricted to persons with a legitimate interest. It specifies which persons are to be considered persons with a legitimate interest (e.g. repairers and recyclers), to which information listed in the battery passport they shall have access, and to what extent they can download, share, publish and re-use that information.
productsFreeText: Industrial batteries, including residential battery energy storage systems; electric vehicle batteries; batteries for light means of transport
objectivesFreeText: Reliable information regarding batteries is essential for their repair, repurposing, remanufacturing, recycling and for deciding between these actions. Being able to make informed choices on the further life and treatment of batteries allows to make the best environmental choice. Some of the necessary information may, however, contain information that is commercially sensitive to the battery manufacturer. Therefore, it is necessary to restrict who can have access to such information and what they can do with it, as already envisaged under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 in notification G/TBT/N/EU/775.

title: Proyecto de Decreto «POR EL CUAL SE HOMOLOGA LA NORMA PARAGUAYA NP 4 020 24, QUE DETERMINA LOS REQUISITOS PARA ALAMBRES DE ACERO AL CARBONO GALVANIZADO DE SECCIÓN OVALADA O CIRCULAR, Y SE DECLARA OBLIGATORIA SU APLICACIÓN EN EL TERRITORIO NACIONAL».
description: The notified draft Decree approves and declares mandatory Paraguayan Standard (NP) No. 4 020 24 (first edition, December 2024) for galvanized carbon steel wire of oval or circular cross-section. It establishes quality, marking, labelling and identification requirements; requires the INTN National Certification Agency (ONC) mark for production, importation, marketing and free-of-charge transfer; and provides for customs controls and MIC oversight. It provides for mandatory application 270 calendar days after promulgation, an additional 90-day period for existing stocks already in the country, and exemptions for specific export maquila operations and samples used for certification.

title: Part 572; Anthropomorphic Test Devices; Test Device for Human Occupant Restraint 50th Percentile Adult Male Dummy (THOR-50M); Extension of Comment Period
description:
In response to a request from the Alliance for Automotive Innovation (Auto Innovators), the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is announcing a 30-day extension of the public comment period for the Supplemental Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (SNPRM) published on 22 September 2026 (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/2043/Add.2). The SNPRM supplements NHTSA's September 2023 notice of proposed rulemaking (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/2043) to amend NHTSA's regulations to include an advanced crash test dummy (the Test Device for Human Occupant Restraint (THOR) 50th percentile adult male) by requesting comment on specifying an additional spine configuration and an alternative to the face foam, and announcing the availability of additional documents. The comment period for the SNPRM was originally scheduled to end on 22 October 2026. It will now end on 21 November 2026.

 

The comment period for the SNPRM published on 22 September 2026 at 91 FR 60068 is extended to 21 November 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 66827, 23 October 2026, Title 49 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 572:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-23/html/2026-21730.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-23/pdf/2026-21730.pdf

 

This extension of comment period and previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/2043 are identified by Docket Number NHTSA-2023-0031. The Docket Folder is available from Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/NHTSA-2023-0031/document and provides access to primary and supporting documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number. WTO Members and their stakeholders are asked to submit comments to the USA TBT Enquiry Point by or before 4pm Eastern Time on 21 November 2026. Comments received by the USA TBT Enquiry Point from WTO Members and their stakeholders will be shared with the regulator and will also be submitted to the Docket on Regulations.gov if received within the comment period.

description: On 7 December 2022, the Government of the Republic of Nicaragua notified, in document G/TBT/N/NIC/174, draft Nicaraguan Mandatory Technical Standard (NTON) No. 09001: Water for human consumption. title: Draft Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine “On Approval of Detailed Rules for Organic Production and Circulation of Organic Products and Repeal of Certain Resolutions of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine”
description:
The draft Resolution establishes Detailed Rules for the organic production and circulation of organic products and in-conversion products. The Rules set out requirements for various categories of organic production, including plant production, livestock production, aquaculture and the production of processed organic products.

The Rules lay down requirements for production methods, the use of products and substances permitted in organic production, the prevention of contamination and mixing with non-organic products, traceability, record-keeping and documentation required for certification. They also establish requirements for labelling, packaging, storage and transport of organic products, as well as specific requirements applicable to different categories of products.

The draft Resolution provides for a transitional period until 1 January 2030 for market operators whose facilities require reconstruction and/or whose land areas need to be expanded to comply with certain production requirements.

title: Medicine labels: Proposed changes to rules for the new standards replacing TGO 91 and TGO 92
description:
Following consultation with stakeholders, the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) introduced 2 new medicine labelling standards in September 2026 to support the safe use of medicines and reflect current labelling practices:

  • Therapeutic Goods (Standard for Labelling of Prescription Medicines) (TGO 115) Order 2026
  • Therapeutic Goods (Standard for Labelling of Non-Prescription Medicines) (TGO 116) Order 2026.

 

These standards were registered on the Federal Register of Legislation on 28 September 2026 and commenced on 30 September 2026. They replace:

  • Therapeutic Goods Order No. 91 - Standard for labels of prescription and related medicines (TGO 91)
  • Therapeutic Goods Order No. 92 - Standard for labels of non-prescription medicines (TGO 92).

 

Medicine sponsors have a 5-year transition period to comply with TGO 115 and TGO 116. During the transition period:

  • prescription medicines may comply with either TGO 91 or TGO 115
  • non-prescription medicines may comply with either TGO 92 or TGO 116.

 

Sponsors may also adopt certain provisions in TGO 115 and TGO 116, in place of corresponding provisions in TGO 91 and TGO 92, before fully transitioning to the new standards. 
 

All medicines released for supply from 1 October 2031 must comply with the new standards.
 

For more information about the transition arrangements and implementation of the new standards, see:

  • New medicine labelling standards
  • Medicine labelling requirements: information for sponsors.

 

Following consideration of stakeholder feedback during consultation, some key changes to measures proposed in the original notification include:

  • extending the transition period from 3 years to 5 years
  • not proceeding with the proposal to stop allowing embossing or debossing of batch numbers and expiry dates on the saleable pack unless they are also printed or clearly contrast with a dark background
  • not proceeding with the proposal to increase access to information about excipient ingredients on labels of medicines that are self-selected by consumers
  • not proceeding with some proposed changes to requirements for declaring gluten on medicine labels.

 

Read more about the results of the consultation and what we planned to do for each proposal on the consultation page: Consultation on proposed changes to labelling of medicines supplied in Australia. After publishing the outcomes, we revised some aspects, including the transition arrangements, following further consideration and engagement with stakeholders.

objectives.name: Protection of human health or safety (TBT)

objectivesFreeText:
Medicine labels give health professionals and consumers important information to help them use medicines safely and correctly. If labels are hard to read or understand, medication errors are more likely.

 

TGO 91 and TGO 92 support the safe and appropriate use of medicines by consumers and health professionals through appropriate labelling. Certain aspects of these labelling requirements need improvement to better support the safe use of medicines, or to give medicine sponsors more clarity. 

 

With TGO 91 and TGO 92 due to sunset on 1 October 2026, we have an opportunity to update and improve requirements for medicine labels.

 

The TGA is seeking feedback to help make sure the proposed updates to labelling requirements for the new standards are clear and support medicine safety.

 

Some key objectives of the proposals include:

  • Align more closely with food labelling rules by updating the substances that must be declared on medicine labels. For example, we propose to require wheat to be declared.
  • Improve information available on medicine labels to help consumers make informed choices. For example, following reports of serious choking related adverse events, we propose adding warnings about large oral dosage forms.
  • Clarify labelling requirements for medicine sponsors.
  • Update rules so that they are fit for purpose, reflect related policy changes since TGO 91/92 were made in 2016, and reflect technological advancements such as increased consumer use of QR codes.
  • Reduce exemptions under Section 14 of the Therapeutic Goods Act 1989 for medicine labels by aligning requirements with accepted label practice.

title: Proposed adoption into the WaterMark Certification Scheme – DR WMTS-543:20xx Pressure dependent stack vent valve
description:
This Specification sets out requirements for a pressure dependent stack vent valve that is installed in the open to atmosphere stack piping. The prime function of the fitting is to minimise heat losses by management of air flows through the stack to the atmosphere. Note: There is no energy efficiency performance criteria for these products as this is dependent on the installation and climatic conditions. 

The Plumbing Code of Australia (PCA) requires that most products intended for use in plumbing and drainage installations in or around buildings to be evaluated and certified to WaterMark product specifications. WaterMark certification to an applicable product specification provides a process to evaluate and authorise products to enable their use in a plumbing and drainage installation. Thus ensuring that the plumbing and drainage products are fit for purpose for which they are intended.

This WaterMark Technical Specification (WMTS) was prepared in accordance with the Manual for the WaterMark Certification Scheme, Appendix 4, Protocol for Developing Product Specifications.

The objective of WaterMark Technical Specification is to enable product certification in accordance with the requirements of the Plumbing Code of Australia (PCA).

hsCodes.name: 848180 - Appliances for pipes, boiler shells, tanks, vats or the like (excl. pressure-reducing valves, valves for the control of pneumatic power transmission, check "non-return" valves and safety or relief valves)

objectives.name: Protection of human health or safety (TBT)

objectivesFreeText:
The objectives of the Scheme are to establish the requirements for product certification and authorisation under Part A5 of the PCA and:
 a) to provide a process to authorise products to enable their use in plumbing and drainage installations as covered by the PCA, and
 b) to ensure that plumbing and drainage products are fit for the purpose for which they are intended and that their use in a plumbing and drainage installation throughout its serviceable life is suitable and does not create significant risks or any likely outcome of:
 (i) personal illness, loss, injury or death;
 (ii) on-site environmental degradation;
 (iii) contamination of the water resource;
 (iv) adverse impact on infrastructure (private or public);
 (v) contamination of water supplies from the point of connection to the points of discharge; or
 (vi) wastage of resources (water and energy).

title: Proposed adoption into the WaterMark Certification Scheme – DR WMTS-544:20xx Appliance for emptying and cleaning a mobile camping waste holding tank (cassette)
description:
This Specification sets out requirements for an Appliance for Emptying and Cleaning a Mobile Camping Waste Holding Tank (Cassette) that has been designed to be user enabled and automatically cleans dedicated cassettes that are utilised in mobile camping applications. The device also adds after the final cleaning process a sanitising fluid and clean water for the removal of odours and to further enhance the degradation of waste material. The Appliance for Emptying and Cleaning a Mobile Camping Waste Holding Tank (Cassette) is intended to be directly connected to the mains cold water supply and sanitary drainage systems. Note: Electrical appliance components shall comply with the relevant requirements of the electrical regulator, where required.

The Plumbing Code of Australia (PCA) requires that most products intended for use in plumbing and drainage installations in or around buildings to be evaluated and certified to WaterMark product specifications. WaterMark certification to an applicable product specification provides a process to evaluate and authorise products to enable their use in a plumbing and drainage installation. Thus ensuring that the plumbing and drainage products are fit for purpose for which they are intended.

This WaterMark Technical Specification (WMTS) was prepared in accordance with the Manual for the WaterMark Certification Scheme, Appendix 4, Protocol for Developing Product Specifications.

objectivesFreeText: Precision class A graduated cylinders used for volume verification may be placed on the market and put into use in the Czech Republic as specified measuring instruments pursuant to Act No 505/1990 on metrology, as amended. Pursuant to this Act, specified measuring instruments are instruments that are included in the list of the types of specified measuring instruments (Decree No 345/2002) and, at the same time, intended (by the manufacturer/importer) for measurements relevant to the protection of public interests in consumer protection, contractual relations, imposition of sanctions, fees, tariffs and taxes, health protection, environmental protection, occupational safety, or the protection of other public interests protected by special legislation. This is therefore a purpose similar to the one defining specified products – non-automatic measuring instruments and scales pursuant to Directives 2014/31/EU and 2014/32/EU. The requirements of this legislation do not apply to measuring instruments not placed on the market in the Czech Republic for the above purposes, defined by Act No 505/1990 on metrology, as amended. The purpose of this notified legislation is to lay down metrological and technical requirements for these specified measuring instruments. This legislation also stipulates tests for type approval and verification of specified measuring instruments of this type.

title: Interpretation of ''Flammable Liquid Fuels'' With Respect to Fuel Additives
description:
The Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) is issuing an interpretive rule that interprets the phrase ''flammable liquid fuels'' as used in the Portable Fuel Container Safety Act of 2020 (PFCSA). Consistent with the plain language of the statute, the Commission interprets this phrase not to include fuel additives that are intended to be added to flammable liquid fuels for the sole purpose of improving engine performance, cleaning engine components, extending engine life, stabilizing fuel, preventing weather effects from fuel, or some similar purpose unrelated to creating heat or power. 

 

The rule is effective on 19 October 2026.

title: Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: Reallocation of Additional 2025 Small Refinery Exemptions
description:
Proposed rule - The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is co-proposing two approaches to revising the existing 2026 and 2027 small refinery exemption (SRE) reallocation volumes under the Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) program in response to a higher volume of 2025 SREs than previously projected when the Agency set the renewable fuel volumes and percentage standards on 1 April 2026. One approach would reallocate the additional 2025 SRE volume equally between the 2026 and 2027 SRE reallocation volumes, while the other approach would reallocate all the additional 2025 SRE volume to the 2027 SRE reallocation volume. Additionally, given the proposed revision to the 2026 standards, this proposed action may extend the existing 2026 compliance reporting deadline of 31 March 2027.

 

The EPA will hold a virtual public hearing on 4 November 2026. The hearing will begin at 9:00 a.m. Eastern Standard Time (EST) and end when all parties who wish to speak have had an opportunity to do so. All hearing attendees (including those who do not intend to provide testimony) must register by sending an email to RFS-Hearing@epa.gov by 28 October 2026. A separate registration form must be submitted for each person attending the hearing. Additional information on how to register can be found at https://www.epa.gov/renewable-fuel-standard/proposed-reallocation-additional-2025-small-refinery-exemptions.

title: Upper C-Band (3.98-4.2 GHz); Expanding Flexible Use of the 3.7 to 4.2 GHz Band
description:
In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) announces that the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) has approved the information collection requirements under OMB Control Number 3060-1272, as adopted in the Commission's Report and Order, Order of Proposed Modification, and Order on Reconsideration, FCC 26-46.

 

Amendatory instructions 26 (47 CFR 27.1412(e)) and 35 (47 CFR 27.1419), published at 91 FR 48700, 31 July 2026, are effective on 19 October 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 66010, 19 October 2026; Title 47 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 27:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-19/html/2026-21324.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-19/pdf/2026-21324.pdf

 

This final rule; announcement of effective date is identified by GN Docket Nos. 18-122 and 25-59; FCC 26-46. Commission documents as well as comments ("filings”) are accessible from the Electronic Comment Filing System (ECFS) at https://www.fcc.gov/ecfs/search/search-filings/results?q=(proceedings.name:(%2225-59%22)). Commission documents are also accessible from the FCC's Electronic Document Management System (EDOCS).

title: Nueva guía para la realización y presentación de estudios de eficacia de productos desinfectantes y sanitizantes de uso sanitario y doméstico
description: The notified technical guide, issued by the Public Health Institute of Chile (ISP), regulates the submission of efficacy studies for the registration of and amendment of health registration certificates for disinfectants and sanitizers for sanitary and household use under Supreme Decree No. 157/2005. The document defines test criteria, minimum requirements for test reports, and specific conditions based on the type of microbial action and field of application (hospital, food, livestock, aquaculture, among others), detailing internationally recognized analytical methodologies (AOAC UNE, ASTM, US-EPA) and revoking the previous exemption for products containing sodium hypochlorite.

title: The Ministerial Decree No.210 /2026 (1 page, in Arabic) and the Ministerial Decree No.229/2026 (1 page, in Arabic) mandating the Egyptian standard ES 9324 for "Liquid synthetic detergents for cleaning of child care articles”.
description:
The Ministerial Decree No. 210 /2026 and the Ministerial Decree No.229/2026 give the producers and importers a six-month transitional period to abide by the Egyptian standard ES 9324 which specifies the requirements for liquid synthetic detergents for washing and cleaning child care articles and supplies, such as feeding bottles and their components, eating and drinking utensils, and children’s toys that may be placed in the child’s mouth and are intended to be used manually with water.

Worth mentioning is that this standard complies with:

 - Regulation (EC) No. 648/2004 of the European parliament and of the council on detergents

- Commission Regulation (EU) No. 10/2011 on plastic materials and articles intended to come into contact with food.

- Regulation (EC) No. 1907/2006 - Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH).

- Regulation (EC) No. 1272/2008 - classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP).

- JIS K 3370/2019 Synthetic Detergents for Kitchen.

- GSO 2238/2021 Liquid Detergent for Manual Dishwashing.

description:
This draft of the Egyptian standard specifies the characteristics, requirements and practical information for aluminium chloride anhydrous, aluminium chloride basic, dialuminium chloride pentahydroxide and aluminium chloride hydroxide sulfate used in the treatment of water intended for human consumption. The standard covers identification, commercial forms, physical and chemical properties, purity criteria, sampling and analytical methods, and rules for labelling, transport, storage and safe handling.

Worth mentioning is that this draft standard is technically identical with EN 17034/2018.

title: Proposal for Amendments to the Legal Inspection Requirements for Fire-retardant Construction Materials
description: The standards used for testing and inspection of calcium silicate boards, slag gypsum boards, fiber cement boards, regenerated fiber cement boards, decorative exterior panel of fiber reinforced cement sidings, cement bonded wood-wool boards, cement bonded wood-flake boards and gypsum boards have been revised. The BSMI proposes to adopt the revised standards to ensure that such products continue to meet applicable safety requirements. In addition, to ensure consistency, the BSMI also proposes to revise the conformity assessment procedure for wallpapers (coverings) from Monitoring Inspection to Type-Approved Batch Inspection (TABI). The alternative procedure of Registration of Product Certification (Modules II+III) remains available for business operators to choose depending on their needs.

titlePlain: Proposal for Amendments to the Legal Inspection Requirements for Fire-retardant Construction Materials
descriptionPlain: The standards used for testing and inspection of calcium silicate boards, slag gypsum boards, fiber cement boards, regenerated fiber cement boards, decorative exterior panel of fiber reinforced cement sidings, cement bonded wood-wool boards, cement bonded wood-flake boards and gypsum boards have been revised. The BSMI proposes to adopt the revised standards to ensure that such products continue to meet applicable safety requirements. In addition, to ensure consistency, the BSMI also proposes to revise the conformity assessment procedure for wallpapers (coverings) from Monitoring Inspection to Type-Approved Batch Inspection (TABI). The alternative procedure of Registration of Product Certification (Modules II+III) remains available for business operators to choose depending on their needs.

title: Powered Air Purifying Respirators (PAPRs) in Underground Mines
description:
In response to a public request, the Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) is reopening the rulemaking record and is scheduling a virtual public hearing on the Agency's proposed rule published on 1 July 2025 (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/2224),  titled, ''Powered Air Purifying Respirators (PAPRs) in Underground Mines.''

 

MSHA is reopening the comment period for the proposed rule published on 1 July 2025, (90 FR 28406) for additional public comments. All new comments must be received or postmarked by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on 8 December 2026.    

 

MSHA will hold a fully virtual public hearing on 17 November 2026 to accept comments from the public on the proposed rule. The event will begin at 9:00 a.m. Eastern Time and will end after the last presenter speaks. Those who wish to speak during the virtual public hearing are asked to register at https://www.msha.gov/regulations/rulemaking/paprs-public-hearing. Speakers should register by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on 13 November 2026. If you do not register in advance and you wish to speak, you will be called after all those who registered have spoken. 
 

91 Federal Register (FR) 65697, 16 October 2026; Title 30 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Parts 57 and 75:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-16/html/2026-21154.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-16/pdf/2026-21154.pdf

 

This reopening of comment period and previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/2224 are identified by Docket Number MSHA-2025-0089. The Docket Folder is available on Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/MSHA-2025-0089/document and provides access to primary documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number. WTO Members and their stakeholders are asked to submit comments to the USA TBT Enquiry Point by or before 4pm Eastern Time on 8 December 2026. Comments received by the USA TBT Enquiry Point from WTO Members and their stakeholders will be shared with MSHA and will also be submitted to the Docket on Regulations.gov if received within the comment period.

title: DEAS 1380: 2026 The handling, storage and distribution of liquefied petroleum gas in domestic, commercial, and industrial Installations — Code of practice — The fuelling of forklift trucks and other gas operated vehicles
description: This draft East African Standard provides recommendations for the equipment used in filling LP gas containers for industrial and commercial equipment e.g. forklift trucks, generators, compressors and other LP gas operated equipment from fixed storage, and for the siting and maintenance of the equipment.  It also covers safety precautions and fuelling procedure.

title: TECHNICAL REGULATION FOR THE MANDATORY PRODUCT CERTIFICATION OF LIGHT ELECTRIC VEHICLES AND BATTERIES FOR LEV APPLICATIONS
description:
This Department Administrative Order (DAO) aims to establish the mandatory product certification requirements for specified Light Electric Vehicles (LEVs) and batteries for LEV applications intended for importation, manufacture, distribution, or sale in the Philippines, to ensure conformity with the applicable Philippine National Standards (PNS) for electrical safety and to protect consumers and the public from hazards associated with electric shock, electrical malfunction, overheating, thermal incidents, fire, and other electrical safety risks arising from the use of such products.
 

This Technical Regulation further aims to support the safe and reliable adoption of electric mobility technologies in the Philippines through the implementation of appropriate mandatory product certification requirements.

title: National technical regulation on electric vehicle charging equipment
description:
Viet Nam informs WTO Members that the Ministry of Industry and Trade adopted Circular No. 61/2026/TT-BCT dated 29 September 2026 promulgating the National technical regulation on electric vehicle charging equipment and charging stations (QCVN 32:2026/BCT). The Circular will enter into force on 1 July 2027.

 

The draft measure was previously notified in G/TBT/N/VNM/340 of 11 March 2025 and G/TBT/N/VNM/340/Add.1 of 13 August 2026. This addendum notifies the adoption and availability of the final text. The adoption date above replaces the proposed adoption dates in the previous notifications.

 

The Regulation establishes technical and management requirements for charging equipment and charging stations, including electrical safety, electromagnetic compatibility, communications, marking and instructions; installation and layout; power supply and connection; metering; monitoring and control; operation and maintenance. It provides for conformity certification, declaration of conformity and conformity marking for charging equipment and for the recognition and use of foreign conformity assessment results in accordance with Vietnamese law. It also sets out documentation, inspection, commissioning and operating requirements for charging stations.

 

The station requirements cover installations in public areas, centralized parking facilities, rest areas and similar locations, subject to the scope and exclusions in Section 1.1. Covered vehicles include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid electric vehicles and similar electric road vehicles with an on-board

title: Draft Circular regulating state management of the quality of medium-risk and high-risk products and goods under the responsibility of the Ministry of Public Security.
description:
Description of content: 
This draft Circular establishes provisions on state management of the quality of medium-risk and high-risk products and goods under the responsibility of the Ministry of Public Security and replaces Circular No. 90/2024/TT-BCA.
The draft covers:
• Scope of regulation, applicable entities and responsibilities of competent state authorities;
• State quality inspection of imported products and goods, including inspection procedures, sampling, testing and handling of non-compliant products;
• Traceability;
• Labelling;
• State quality inspection of products and goods during production and circulation on the market;
• Conformity assessment activities and the designation and management of conformity assessment bodies;
• Recognition of conformity assessment results issued by foreign organizations in accordance with Vietnamese law;
• Responsibilities of relevant authorities, conformity assessment bodies, organizations and individuals;
• Implementation and transitional provisions.
The draft applies to relevant state management agencies, organizations and individuals engaged in the production, importation and trading of products and goods under the responsibility of the Ministry of Public Security, as well as conformity assessment bodies and other relevant organizations and individuals.

title: The draft Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine “On Amendments to the Procedure for State Quality Control of Medicines Imported into Ukraine”
description:
Ukraine notifies the adoption of Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 1254 “On Amendments to the Procedure for State Quality Control of Medicines Imported into Ukraine” of 13 October 2026.

The Resolution was officially published and entered into force on 16 October 2026. 

Сompared with the notified draft, the adopted Resolution includes provisions on:

the issuance of quality conclusions based on GMP certificates issued by the regulatory authorities of specified countries; 

the visual inspection of previously imported batches of medicines upon their re-importation; 

specific arrangements for the laboratory testing of certain immunobiological products based on official batch release; 

the use of packaging materials compliant with the registration dossier in force before the re-registration of a medicinal product. 

The adopted Resolution also shortens certain time limits for visual inspection and the issuance of quality conclusions and further specifies the requirements for submitting photographic evidence and cargo inspection results during martial law.

The Resolution will remain in force until 1 January 2027, when Law of Ukraine No. 2469-IX “On Medicines” becomes effective.

title: Draft Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine “On Approval of Common Criteria for the Justification of Claims Used in Relation to Cosmetic Products”
description:
The draft Resolution provides for the approval of Common criteria for the justification of claims (product claims) used in relation to cosmetic products. The Criteria establish the requirements for substantiating such claims and the procedure for applying these requirements.
The Criteria shall apply to claims in the form of texts, names, trademarks, images, graphic or other signs that explicitly or implicitly convey products characteristics or functions in the labelling, making available on the market and advertising of cosmetic products. It shall apply to any claim, irrespective of the medium or type of marketing tool used, the product functions claimed, and the target audience.
The responsible person shall ensure that claims in relation to cosmetic products comply  with the established Criteria and are consistent with the documentation proving the effect claimed for the cosmetic product.
The Criteria address six aspects: legal compliance, truthfulness, evidentiary support, honesty, fairness and informed decision-making.
The draft Resolution also establishes that cosmetic products placed on the market before 31 July 2027 and whose claims do not comply with the newly established Criteria, may continue to be made available on the market until 3 August 2030.

title: Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (26-1)
description:
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is issuing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. The SNURs require persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of any of these chemical substances for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification; made an appropriate determination regarding that notification; and taken such actions as required by that determination.

 

This rule is effective on 14 December 2026. For purposes of judicial review, this rule shall be promulgated at 1 p.m. (EST) on 29 October 2026.

title: Draft Circular amending and supplementing a number of articles of Circular No. 07/2022/TT-BYT of the Minister of Health prescribing medicinal products subject to bioequivalence studies and requirements for bioequivalence study reports in applications for marketing authorization of medicinal products in Viet Nam
description:
This draft Circular amends Clause 3 of Article 14 and Clause 2 of Article 15 of Circular No. 07/2022/TT-BYT. It sets the deadline for publication of medicinal products with documentation demonstrating bioequivalence at 1 November 2026 (1 November 2028 for products containing active ingredients no. 13–26 of Appendix I to Circular No. 07/2022/TT-BYT or in enteric-coated dosage forms.

Article 1. Amendments and supplements to a number of articles of Circular No. 07/2022/TT-BYT dated 5 September 2022 of the Minister of Health prescribing medicinal products subject to bioequivalence studies and requirements for bioequivalence study reports in applications for marketing authorization of medicinal products in Viet Nam

1. Clause 3 of Article 14 is amended and supplemented as follows:

3. For medicinal products that have been granted marketing authorization and contain active ingredients or are in dosage forms subject to bioequivalence testing in accordance with this Circular:

a) By no later than 1 November 2026, medicinal products must be published as products with documentation demonstrating bioequivalence, except for medicinal products containing active ingredients listed from item 13 to item 26 of Appendix I issued together with this Circular, or medicinal products in enteric-coated dosage forms, for which the publication deadline is no later than 1 November 2028.

If a medicinal product has not been published by the prescribed deadline, the release of batches for circulation in Viet Nam and the importation of the medicinal product into Viet Nam shall be subject to Point b of this Clause.

The order and procedures for publication shall comply with the Circular governing the marketing authorization of medicinal products and medicinal ingredients;

b) By the deadline prescribed in Point a of this Clause, for medicinal products that have not been published:

- Where the publication dossier has not been validly received by the competent authority, the manufacturer shall not release the batch of the medicinal product for circulation in Viet Nam; the registration holder shall not place that batch on the market in Viet Nam and shall not import into Viet Nam any medicinal product that has not yet been shipped from the port of departure in the exporting country, until the dossier has been validly received.

- Where the publication dossier has been validly received by the competent authority, the manufacturer may continue to release the batch of the medicinal product for circulation in Viet Nam; the registration holder may continue to place that batch on the market in Viet Nam and continue to import the medicinal product into Viet Nam during the assessment period. If a written conclusion that the dossier does not meet the requirements or a written decision returning the dossier is issued, the manufacturer shall not release the batch of the medicinal product for circulation in Viet Nam; the registration holder shall not place that batch on the market in Viet Nam and shall not import into Viet Nam any medicinal product that has not yet been shipped from the port of departure in the exporting country, from the date of issuance of the written document until the medicinal product has been published.

The valid receipt of the dossier does not replace the obligation to have the medicinal product published in accordance with Point a of this Clause.

c) Domestically manufactured medicinal products whose batches were released for circulation in Viet Nam before the date on which further batch releases are prohibited under Point b of this Clause may continue to circulate until their expiry dates. Imported medicinal products that were shipped from the port of departure in the exporting country before the date on which further importation is prohibited under Point b of this Clause may continue to be imported and circulated until their expiry dates.”

2. Clause 2 of Article 15 is amended as follows:

2. For medicinal products for which marketing authorization applications were submitted before the obligation to submit bioequivalence study reports arises under Clause 1 or Clause 2 of Article 14 of this Circular, the submission of supplementary bioequivalence study reports shall not be required before the marketing authorization is granted.

After marketing authorization has been granted, the registration holder shall comply with Clause 3 of Article 14 of this Circular. Where the date on which marketing authorization is granted falls before the publication deadline prescribed in Point a of Clause 3 of Article 14, the publication deadline shall be the deadline prescribed in Point a of Clause 3 of Article 14 of this Circular. Where the date on which marketing authorization is granted falls on or after the publication deadline prescribed in Point a of Clause 3 of Article 14, the release of batches for circulation in Viet Nam and the importation of medicinal products into Viet Nam shall, from the date of grant, be subject to Points b and c of Clause 3 of Article 14 of this Circular.

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine “On Approval of Amendments to the Procedure for Conducting Clinical Studies (Trials) of Medicinal Products”
description:
The draft Order provides for amendments to the Procedure for Conducting Clinical Studies (Trials) of Medicinal Products, approved by Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine No. 184 of 16 February 2026 “Certain Issues on the Procedure for Conducting Clinical Studies (Trials) of Medicinal Products”.
The amendments aim to eliminate regulatory barriers to conducting clinical trials in Ukraine and update the applicable procedural requirements in accordance the provisions of the Law of Ukraine No. 2469-IX “On Medicines”. 
The key amendments include:
clarifying requirements for Phase I clinical trials and bioequivalence studies conducted on an outpatient basis, including intensive care unit (ICU) support, and updating quality assurance and compliance requirements for bioanalytical laboratories;
allowing multilingual labelling, provided that the text is identical in all languages, and revising the documentation requirements for clinical trial applications;
introducing an accelerated review procedure, including preliminary review within three business days, at the applicant’s request, and specifying the applicable review timelines, conditions for conditional decisions and preparatory steps before a trial may commence;
establishing clear timelines, ranging from 10 to 60 days, and streamlining procedures for reviewing substantial modifications to ongoing clinical trials.

title: Trichloroethylene (TCE); Regulation Under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA); Compliance Date Extensions
description:
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is proposing to extend certain compliance dates applicable to certain entities subject to the regulation of trichloroethylene (TCE) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) until 31 December 2027, including for certain chemical processors in meeting the prohibition compliance deadline for the processing of TCE, industrial and commercial use of TCE as a processing aid, and associated wastewater disposal; and for refrigerant manufacturers in meeting the compliance deadline for phasing down TCE feedstock in the production of HFC-134a. This proposed compliance extension would allow for necessary and reasonable transition periods for regulated entities under TSCA section 6(d).

 

Comments must be received on or before 13 November 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 65148, 14 October 2026; Title 40 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 751:

title: Reconsideration of the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program
description:
Interim final rule; request for comment - The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is taking interim final action to extend the reporting deadline under the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Rule for reporting year 2025 data from 30 October 2026, to 10 March 2027. This final action only changes the reporting deadline for annual greenhouse gas reports for reporting year 2025 and makes no other changes to the rule. The EPA is requesting comments on all aspects of this interim final rule.

 

This interim final rule is effective on 14 October 2026. 

Comments on this rule must be received on or by 30 November 2026.    

If anyone contacts the EPA requesting a public hearing on or before 19 October 2026, the Agency will hold a virtual public hearing. To request a virtual public hearing, contact the public hearing team at (888) 372-8699 or by email at NRDpublichearing@epa.gov. If requested, the hearing will be held via virtual platform on 29 October 2026. The EPA will provide further information about the hearing on its website (https://www.epa.gov/ghgreporting) if a hearing is requested.
