title: Draft Law Amending and Supplementing a Number of Articles of the Law on Prevention and Control of Tobacco Harms
description:
The Draft Law comprises 3 Articles:
Description of content: The Draft Law comprises 3 Articles:
Article 1. Amendments and supplements to a number of articles of the Law on Prevention and Control of Tobacco Harms:
1. Amends Clause 1, adds Clauses 1a, 1b, 1c, 1d and 1đ after Clause 1, and adds Clause 10 to Article 2, thereby amending and supplementing the definitions of tobacco, electronic cigarettes, heated tobacco products, electronic devices, specialized tobacco products, other tobacco products and display of tobacco products.
2. Amends Clause 4 of Article 3 to supplement the policy of guaranteeing the right to live and work in a smoke-free environment, in particular for vulnerable groups.
3. Adds Clause 5 to Article 5 to ensure transparency and freedom from the influence of tobacco industry interests in the development and implementation of policies.
4. Amends and supplements Article 9 to expand the prohibited acts applicable to electronic cigarettes, heated tobacco products and other tobacco products.
5. Amends and supplements Article 19 on licensing management for the production, trading and importation of tobacco products and tobacco raw materials.
6. Amends Clause 4 of Article 21 on the management of the assignment and licensing of industrial property rights in respect of tobacco products.
7. Amends Point d of Clause 1, Clause 2 and Clause 3 of Article 22 on management of domestic tobacco consumption volume.
8. Adds Article 23a providing for establishment-specific standards applicable to cigars, shredded tobacco and thuốc lào (water-pipe tobacco).
9. Amends Article 25 to strengthen control over the sale of tobacco products to persons under 18 years of age and in areas surrounding schools and health facilities.
10. Amends and supplements a number of terms to align with the new organizational structure and names of State management agencies by sector.
11. Deletes the phrase "inspection" in Point e, Clause 2 of Article 5; deletes the phrase "except for establishments specified in Point b, Clause 2 of this Article" in Point b, Clause 1 of Article 11; and deletes the phrase "colleges, universities and academies" in Point b, Clause 2 of Article 11.
12. Repeals Clause 2 and Clause 4 of Article 17; Clause 6 of Article 21; Point c, Clause 1 of Article 22; and Point a, Clause 1 of Article 25.
Article 2. Effect:
1. This Law shall enter into force on 1 July 2027.
2. Amends, supplements and repeals a number of provisions in laws related to prevention and control of tobacco harms.
Article 3. Transitional provisions: 
1. The current limit of one pack, one carton or one box per tobacco brand for display shall continue to apply for six months after this Law takes effect; 
2. From 1 March 2027, requirements for tobacco trading and sale licenses, and for the establishment and operation of tobacco cessation and counselling services, are repealed; 
3. From 1 January 2028, producers of cigars, shredded tobacco and waterpipe tobacco must develop and publish establishment-specific standards; importers must declare applicable standards.

title: Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine No. 184 of 16 February 2026  “Certain Issues of the Procedure for Conducting Clinical Studies (Trials) of Medicinal Products"
description:
Ukraine notifies Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine No. 184 of 16 February 2026, “Certain Issues Concerning the Procedure for Conducting Clinical Studies (Trials) of Medicinal Products”.

The Order aims to eliminate regulatory barriers to conducting clinical trials in Ukraine and update the applicable procedural requirements in line with the provisions of Law of Ukraine No. 2469-IX of 28 July 2022 “On Medicines”.

In particular, the Order approves the Procedure for Conducting Clinical Studies (Trials) of Medicinal Products and the Requirements for the Form and Content of Informed Consent for Participation in Clinical Studies (Trials).

The Procedure for Conducting Clinical Studies (Trials) of Medicinal Products establishes the main requirements for conducting clinical trials of medicinal products in Ukraine, including advanced therapy medicinal products, combined advanced therapy medicinal products, bioavailability and bioequivalence studies, and international multicentre clinical trials, involving patients or healthy volunteers.

The Order was developed taking into account the provisions of Directive 2001/83/EC, Regulation (EU) No 536/2014, Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 and Commission Directive 2005/28/EC, including its provisions on the authorisation of the manufacture or import of investigational medicinal products, with the aim of regulating the conduct of clinical trials of medicinal products and the assessment of clinical trial documentation.

title: Use of Salt Substitutes To Reduce the Sodium Content in Standardized Foods
description:
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) is issuing a final rule to amend our standard of identity regulations that specify salt (sodium chloride) as a required or optional ingredient to permit the use of salt substitutes in standardized foods, to reduce the sodium content. Reducing sodium may help reduce the risk of hypertension, a major risk factor for heart disease and stroke. The rule will help support a healthier food supply by providing flexibility to facilitate industry innovation in the production of standardized foods lower in sodium while maintaining the basic nature and essential characteristics of the foods.

 

This rule is effective 14 December 2026. The incorporation by reference of certain material listed in this rule is approved by the Director of the Federal Register as of 14 December 2026. Submit either electronic or written/paper objections or requests for a hearing on amendments to standards of identity for dairy products in parts 131 and 133 (21 CFR parts 131 and 133) under this final rule by 12 November 2026. See section VI for further information on the filing of objections on amendments to standards of identity for dairy products in parts 131 and 133.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 65040, 13 October 2026; Title 21 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Parts 130, 131, 133, 136, 137, 139, 145, 150, 155, 156, 158, 161, 163, 166, 168, and 169:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-13/html/2026-20848.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-13/pdf/2026-20848.pdf

 

This final rule and the proposed rule notified as G/TBT/N/USA/1982 are identified by Docket Number FDA-2022-N-2226. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number.

title: Draft Commission Implementing Regulation concerning the non-renewal of approval of the active substance triclopyr, in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council, and amending Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 540/2011
description:
This draft Commission Implementing Regulation provides that the approval of the active substance triclopyr is not renewed in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009. Member States shall withdraw authorisations for plant protection products containing triclopyr as an active substance. The non-renewal of approval is based on the first evaluation of the substance for use as a pesticide active substance in the EU under Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009. The substance was formerly assessed and approved under Directive 91/414/ EEC.

This decision only concerns the placing on the market of this substance and plant protection products containing it. Following non-approval and the expiry of all grace periods for stocks of products containing this substance, separate action may be taken on MRLs and a separate notification will be made in accordance with SPS procedures.

objectives.name: Protection of human health or safety (TBT)
Protection of animal or plant life or health (TBT)

objectivesFreeText:
In order for an active substance to be approved in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 (concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market), it must be demonstrated that the substance is not harmful to human health, animal health or the environment. Criteria are listed in Article 4 of the Regulation (and also detailed in Annex II thereto) which must be met to enable approval. 

During the evaluation and peer-review of triclopyr, a number of concerns and areas that could not be finalised were identified. These are detailed in the conclusion of the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA). 

In particular, a high acute and long-term risk to mammals and a high risk to non-target arthropods was identified. Furthermore, the consumer risk assessment is provisional pending the data gaps related to storage stability data. The risk assessment for aquatic organisms could not be finalised since suitable toxicity data were not available for all taxa. Finally, no quantified risk assessment was available for spot applications where applications are indicated not to exceed 20% of the treated surface area.

These concerns mean that triclopyr does not meet the approval criteria as outlined in Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009.

Existing authorisations will need to be withdrawn; Member States must withdraw existing plant protection products containing triclopyr at the latest by 6 months from the date of entry into force. A period of grace in line with Article 46 of Regulation 1107/2009 is allowed for and shall expire at the latest 12 months from the entry into force (allowing for a final season of use).

title: Draft Decree amending and supplementing a number of articles of the Government’s Decree No. 22/2026/ND-CP dated January 16, 2026, Decree No. 37/2026/ND-CP dated January 23, 2026, and Decree No. 127/2026/ND-CP dated April 6, 2026
description:
This draft Decree amends and supplements several articles of Decree No. 22/2026/ND-CP, Decree No. 37/2026/ND-CP, and Decree No. 127/2026/ND-CP regarding the decentralization, reduction, and simplification of administrative procedures and business conditions, as well as the refinement of certain regulations, forms, and transitional provisions. 
The subjects of application include state agencies, organizations, and individuals governed by the three Decrees, as well as agencies, organizations, and individuals involved in the implementation of the amended and supplemented provisions.
1) Content regarding the amendment and supplementation of certain articles of Decree No. 22/2026/NĐ-CP: 
(a) Decentralization and simplification: certificates of registration for testing, inspection,
certification and confirmation of utility value/verification activities are issued by the
Chairperson of the provincial People's Committee [Resolution No. 20/2026/NQ-CP, Appendix I];
re-issuance procedures for accreditation activities are simplified [Appendix II - confirm].
(b) Conformity assessment bodies (CABs): applications declare only the field and scope of
activity (e.g. field "chemistry", scope "agricultural products"). Within a registered scope,
CABs update their information (at minimum product names, test names and personnel) in the National Database on Standards, Metrology and Quality before performing the activity, without a registration procedure for amendment; extending the registered scope still requires registration. Authorities reuse data already available in national databases, and applicants submit documents only where data cannot be retrieved. Risk-based, data-driven inspection of CABs is strengthened. Forms are revised accordingly.
(c) Standards and technical regulations: updated provisions on the TBT Network, national
technical committees, consultation on the draft national standards plan (15 days) and on draft national standards (at least 60 days; at least 30 days in urgent cases relating to health, safety or the environment); the simplified procedure for technical regulations (Art. 29) is clarified and distinguished from the standard procedure (Art. 27).
2) Content regarding amendments and supplements to a number of articles of Decree No. 37/2026/ND-CP:
- Abolish the administrative procedure for re-issuance of the designation decision as prescribed in Appendix II issued together with Resolution No. 20/2026/NQ-CP.
- Amend and supplement regulations on goods labelling and inspection of imported goods to align with practical implementation over the recent period.
- Amend and supplement regulations on testing activities serving conformity certification for high-risk goods to ensure consistent management between domestically produced goods and imported goods.
- Amend and supplement regulations regarding the designation of conformity assessment bodies with a view to reducing and simplifying business conditions. Specifically, the draft removes the requirement for testers to possess at least two years of work experience in the testing field for which designation is sought; instead, tester competence will be verified and demonstrated through professional training certificates, internal test method approvals, and accreditation assessment results under ISO/IEC 17025. Additionally, requirements for testers, inspectors, and assessors are supplemented to address situations involving changes or additions to the scope of designation.
- Add a transitional mechanism to Article 98 of Decree No. 37/2026/NĐ-CP to fully and stably institutionalize the mechanism for using labels and packaging bearing a former name in cases where an enterprise changes its name without altering its legal entity status or the entity responsible for the goods, in accordance with Resolution No. 39/2026/NQ-CP.
3) Content regarding the amendment and supplementation of several articles of Decree No. 127/2026/NĐ-CP:
- Registration of Halal certification bodies is decentralized to the Chairperson of the provincial People's Committee (Conclusion No. 18-KL/TW; Notice No. 185/TB-VPCP).

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine “On Approval of the Procedure for the Importation and Circulation of Unregistered Medicinal Products in Ukraine”
description:
The draft Order proposes to approve the Procedure for the Importation and Circulation of Unregistered Medicinal Products in Ukraine in order to:

establish a uniform mechanism and regulate the procedures for the importation into Ukraine and circulation of unregistered medicinal products;

specify the list of documents to be submitted to obtain confirmation for the importation of an unregistered medicinal product and the procedure for their review;

establish specific cases in which unregistered medicinal products may be imported;

lay down specific arrangements for the importation of unregistered medicinal products in emergencies that may pose a threat to public health.

The draft Order prohibits the importation and use of falsified and substandard unregistered medicinal products, as well as medicinal products that are not registered in Ukraine and for which a regulatory decision to withdraw or suspend the marketing authorisation on safety grounds has been issued in the EU and/or the country of manufacture.

The remaining shelf life of unregistered medicinal products imported into Ukraine must be at least half of the shelf life specified by the manufacturer where the specified shelf life is  less than one year, or at least six months where the specified shelf life is more than one year.

Upon the entry into force of this Order, Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine No. 237 of 26 April 2011 “On Approval of the Procedure for Importation of Unregistered Medicinal Products, Reference Standards and Reagents into the Territory of Ukraine" shall cease to have effect.

title: Draft National European Train Control System Mandatory Standard
description: This is a new measure to standardise specifications for the use of European Train Control System digital train control signalling so that they can be interoperable between rail networks. The standard includes both trackside and on-board requirements. Australian ministers have agreed to a European Train Control System pathway for Australia's National Network for Interoperability.

objectivesFreeText: This standard will support seamless train movement across Australia’s states and territories and various rail networks by standardising the implementation of European Train Control System digital signalling so that it is interoperable between networks. Moreover, fragmentation of digital signalling would create barriers to productivity and the efficient movement of passengers and freight as trains move between rail networks.

title: Regulation of The Halal Product Assurance Organizing Agency of The Republic of Indonesia Number 4 of 2026 Concerning Conformity Verification of Foreign Halal Products Entering The Territory of Indonesia
description: This Regulation establishes the requirements and procedures for verifying the conformity of imported products with Indonesia’s halal product assurance requirements. Verification comprises administrative document checks and limited physical conformity inspections conducted by inspection bodies designated by BPJPH at the loading warehouse in the country of loading and/or origin prior to shipment. These activities cover conformity with halal certificates or foreign halal certificate registration numbers, halal labelling or non-halal information requirements, import documentation, and other applicable halal product assurance requirements. The results are documented in a Halal Product Verification Report (LPPH), which is valid for a single shipment or importation and is required upon submission of the import customs declaration. The Regulation further stipulates requirements for the designation of inspection bodies, application procedures, fees, exemptions for specified categories of goods, reporting obligations, monitoring and evaluation, and administrative sanctions. It shall enter into force 30 days after the date of promulgation.
productsFreeText: This regulation applies to all goods and services subject to the phased implementation of mandatory halal certification under Government Regulation No. 42 of 2024 concerning the Implementation of Halal Product Assurance, including food, beverages, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, chemical products, biological products, genetically engineered products, consumer goods used, utilized or consumed by the public, and  services related to slaughtering, processing, storage, packaging, distribution, sales, and serving.

title: Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Flavourings and Certain Food Ingredients with Flavouring Properties for Use in And on Foods
description:
The Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Flavourings and certain food ingredients with flavouring properties for use in and on foods, which was notified through G/TBT/N/TUR/223 (22 November 2024), was adopted and published in the Official Gazette dated 14 September 2026 and numbered 33370. 

 

The Regulation establishes provisions on food flavourings, food ingredients with flavouring properties, the source materials used in their production, their conditions of use and labelling principles, as well as production conditions for smoke flavourings. 

 

The Regulation entered into force on the date of its publication. Food business operators within the scope of the Regulation are required to comply with its provisions by 31 December 2026. Products placed on the market before 31 December 2026 may remain on the market until the end of their shelf life in accordance with the transitional provisions. Certain flavouring substances listed in the transitional provision may no longer be placed on the market, used in food production or imported as of 31 December 2026.
productsFreeText: Food flavourings and certain food ingredients with flavouring properties

title: Ministry of the Environment Decree on essential technical requirements for the mechanical connectors of copper pipes intended for the water supply systems of buildings, 2018/639/FIN
description:
The new EU drinking water Directive (EU) 2020/2184 and its hygiene requirements have been implemented through legislation of the Ministry of Social Affairs and Health. Regulation overlapping with the drinking water Directive and its national implementation must be repealed from the legislation of the Ministry of the Environment.

 

The Decree issues minimum requirements in Finland for the mechanical connectors of copper pipes intended for the supply of drinking water and hot water and which are located in buildings and properties. The provisions of the current Decree (481/2019) on the suitability for the conveyance of domestic water are repealed. In other respects, no changes are made to the Decree.

description:
The draft Order proposes to amend the Requirements for milk, dairy products and spreadable fats intended for human consumption, approved by Order of the Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture of Ukraine No. 801 "On Approval of Requirements for Milk, Dairy Products and Spreadable Fats" of 19 January 2026 (notified in document G/TBT/N/UKR/376), in particular with regard to clarifying:

the definition of the term "butter";

the permissible deviations from the declared fat content in spreadable fats by establishing the relevant tolerances in percentage points.

The draft Order is expected to enter into force on 1 January 2029, simultaneously with the entry into force of the Order No. 801 of 19 January 2026.

The draft Order is also notified under the SPS Agreement.

title: Energy Conservation Program: Test Procedures for Commercial Warm Air Furnaces
description:
The Department of Energy (''DOE'' or ''the Department'') is withdrawing the test procedure for commercial warm air furnaces adopted under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act, specifically appendix B, ''Uniform Test Method for Measurement of the Energy Efficiency of Commercial Warm Air Furnaces (Thermal Efficiency Two).'' Upon reconsideration, DOE has determined that appendix B would have an uncertain increase in representativeness that does not outweigh the likely increase in burden. DOE has also determined that withdrawing the appendix B test procedure would be consistent with the proposed Process Rule, which states that for certain categories of equipment, including CWAFs, DOE will adopt the industry test procedure, as contemplated by EPCA, except in very limited circumstances. Commercial warm air furnaces will continue to be subject to the testing requirements of appendix A, ''Uniform Test Method for Measurement of the Energy Efficiency of Commercial Warm Air Furnaces (Thermal Efficiency).''

 

The effective date of this rule is 7 December 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 64105, 7 October 2026; Title 10 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 431:

title: Draft National Technical Regulation on Petroleum Retail Service Stations
description:
The draft National Technical Regulation prescribes technical requirements for the design, construction, installation, modification, expansion, conversion, inspection, testing, commissioning and safe operation of petroleum retail service stations located on land and on water.

The draft covers, among others:

- Classification of petroleum retail service stations according to total storage capacity and levels of technical safety assurance;

- General requirements for the layout and operation of service stations;

- Hazardous area classification and requirements for equipment installed or used in hazardous areas;

- Storage tanks for petroleum products, including requirements for double-wall tanks or equivalent secondary containment for newly installed or replaced tanks under specified safety levels;

- Fuel piping systems, including underground and above-ground piping, leak detection and emergency shut-off arrangements;

- Fuel dispensers and fuel dispensing systems;

- Electrical installations, grounding, lightning protection and static electricity control;

- Fire prevention and firefighting equipment and emergency response arrangements;

- Water supply, drainage, wastewater and environmental protection requirements;

- Stage I and Stage II vapor recovery systems;

- Requirements for electric vehicle charging stations, battery swapping stations, battery energy storage systems and solar photovoltaic systems installed at petroleum retail service stations;

- Minimum safety distances between service station facilities and surrounding buildings and infrastructure;

- Inspection, testing, commissioning and documentation requirements; 

- Responsibilities of regulatory authorities and petroleum traders operating service stations.

The draft applies to organizations and individuals involved in the construction, modification, operation and management of petroleum retail service stations, petroleum traders and other relevant organizations and individuals.
productsFreeText:
Petroleum retail service stations and equipment, systems and facilities used for the storage and dispensing of petroleum products, including underground petroleum storage tanks, fuel piping systems, fuel dispensers, vapor recovery systems, electrical equipment, fire prevention and firefighting equipment, and related auxiliary facilities.

This draft applies to petroleum retail service stations serving road and waterway transport, including fixed and floating service stations.

title: Proyecto de “Reforma Parcial a la Normativa Técnica Sanitaria para el análisis de control de calidad posregistro o posnotificación de los productos de uso y consumo humano sujetos a control y vigilancia sanitaria”
description: The notified draft partial amendment to the Technical Health Regulations for the post-registration or post-notification quality control analysis of products for human use and consumption subject to health controls and surveillance establishes the procedure and conditions under which the National Agency for Health Surveillance, Regulation and Control (ARCSA), Doctor Leopoldo Izquieta Pérez, will use laboratory analysis services provided by conformity assessment bodies (CABs) accredited by the Ecuadorian Accreditation Service (SAE) and registered with ARCSA, for the post-registration or post-notification quality control of products for human use and consumption subject to health controls and surveillance.G/TBT/N/ECU/560- 2 - Compliance with the Technical Health Regulations is mandatory for ARCSA officials; for holders of a health registration, mandatory health authorization, health notification or a unique GMP code; and for CABs accredited by the SAE and registered with ARCSA that conduct the post-registration or post-notification quality control of products for human use and consumption subject to health controls and surveillance.

title: The Egyptian standard ES 1725 for "Salted fish" (16 pages, in Arabic).
description:
Products covered: ICS: 67.120.30 (Fish and fishery products). 

This addendum concerns the notification of the Ministerial Decree No.209/2026 (2 pages, in Arabic) that gives the producers and importers a six -month transitional period to abide by the Egyptian standard ES 1725 for "Salted fish" (16 pages, in Arabic).

It should be noted that the Ministerial Decree No. 130 /2005 (11 pages, in Arabic) which was formerly notified in G/TBT/N/EGY/1 dated 14 December 2005 and the Ministerial Decree No. 256/2016 which was formerly notified in G/TBT/N/EGY/1/Add.1 dated 15 August 2016, mandated among others the earlier versions of this Egyptian Standard and the draft of this Egyptian standard was formerly notified in G/TBT/N/EGY/1/Add.36 dated 8 April 2026.

Worth mentioning is that this standard complies with Codex standard CXS 244 "Salted Atlantic Herring and Salted Sprat" adopted in 2004, amended in 2011, 2013, 2016, 2018 and 2024.

Producers and importers are kept informed of any amendments in the Egyptian Standard through the publication of administrative orders in the official gazette.

Date of adoption: 21/9/ 2026.

Date of entry into force: The day following the date of publication in the official gazette.

title: The Egyptian standard ES 1589 for "General standard for bottled/ packaged drinking waters (other than natural mineral waters) “(partial amendment in 1 page, in Arabic).
description:
Products covered: (ICS code: 13.060.10) Water of natural resources

This addendum concerns the notification of the Ministerial Decree No. 209/2026 (2 pages, in Arabic) that gives the producers and importers a six -month transitional period to abide by the Egyptian standard ES 1589 for "General standard for bottled/ packaged drinking waters (other than natural mineral waters) “(partial amendment in 1 page, in Arabic).

This addendum concerns the notification of the Ministerial Decree No. 209 /2026 (2 pages, in Arabic) that gives the producers and importers a six -month transitional period to abide by the Egyptian Standard ES 8205-1 "General requirements for traditional cigarette alternatives – Part 1: Electronic Cigarettes – e- Liquid"(12 pages, in Arabic) (partial amendment in 1 page, in Arabic).

It should be noted that the Ministerial Decree No. 101/2019 (2 pages, in Arabic) which was formerly notified in G/TBT/N/EGY/207/Add.1 dated 15 May 2019, the Ministerial Decree No. 222/2021 (1 page, in Arabic) which was formerly notified in G/TBT/N/EGY/207/Add.2 dated 31 August 2021, the Ministerial Decree No. 503/2023 (2 pages, in Arabic) which was formerly notified in G/TBT/N/EGY/207/Add.3 dated 4 April 2024 mandated among others the earlier versions of this Standard and the draft of this Egyptian Standard was formerly notified in G/TBT/N/EGY/207/Add.4 dated 15 April 2026.

Worth mentioning is that this standard has been partially amended as follows:

  • Item No.3/6 to be: (The volume of liquid in the cartridge (clause 2/4) that contains the e-liquid and is intended for single use and to be fitted on its own heating device shall not exceed 20 ml).
  • Item No.3/7 to be: (The capacity of the e-liquid container integrated within the same product shall not exceed 20 ml).

title: The Ministerial Decree No.208/2026 (2 pages, in Arabic) mandating the Egyptian standard ES 5813 for “Household and Similar Electrical Appliances - Safety - Particular requirements for appliances for heating liquids”.
description:
The Ministerial Decree No. 208/2026 gives the producers and importers a twelve - month transitional period to abide by the Egyptian standard ES 5813 that deals with the safety of electrical appliances for heating liquids for household and similar purposes, their rated voltage being not more than 250 V including direct current (DC) supplied appliances and battery-operated appliances. Some appliances in this standard are used for heating food.
Examples of appliances that are within the scope of this standard are:
– Coffee-makers;
– Cooking pans;
– Egg boilers;
– Feeding-bottle heaters;
– Kettles and other appliances for boiling water, having a rated capacity not exceeding 10 l;
– Milk heaters;
– Pressure cookers having a rated cooking pressure not exceeding 140 kPa and a rated capacity not exceeding 10 l;
– Rice cookers;
– Slow cookers;
– Steam cookers;
– Soy milk makers;
– Tea maker;
– Wash boilers;
– Yoghurt makers.
Appliances can have more than one function.
Appliances intended for normal household and similar use and that can also be used by laypersons in shops, in light industry and on farms, are within the scope of this standard. Examples of such appliances are glue pots with a water jacket, livestock feed boilers and sterilizers.
If the appliance is intended to be used professionally to process food for commercial consumption, the appliance is not considered to be for household and similar use only.
As far as is practicable, this standard deals with the common hazards presented by appliances that are encountered by all persons in and around the home. However, in general, it does not take into account
– Persons (including children) whose physical, sensory or mental capabilities; or lack of experience and knowledge prevents them from using the appliance safely without supervision or instruction;
– Children playing with the appliance.
Attention is drawn to the fact that
– For appliances intended to be used in vehicles or on board ships or aircraft, additional requirements can be necessary;
– In many countries additional requirements are specified by the national health authorities, the national authorities responsible for the protection of labour, the national water supply authorities and similar authorities and additional national requirements for pressure vessels are specified for pressure cookers.

Worth mentioning is that this standard is technically identical with IEC 60335-2-15:2024.

title: Low-voltage switchgear and controlgear – Part 2: Circuit-breakers
description:
This document applies to circuit-breakers, intended to be installed and operated by instructed or skilled persons, the main contacts of which are intended to be connected to circuits, the rated voltage of which does not exceed 1 000 V AC or 1 500 V DC; it also contains additional requirements for integrally fused circuit-breakers.

This document also applies to circuit-breakers with ratings at or below 1 000 V AC, additionally having one or more ratings above 1 000 V AC but not exceeding 1 500 V AC.

It applies whatever the rated currents, the method of construction or the proposed applications of the circuit-breakers may be.

Circuit-breakers per this document are suitable for isolation.

The requirements for circuit-breakers which are also intended to provide residual current protection are contained in Annex B.

Additional requirements for circuit-breakers intended for connection of aluminium conductors are contained in Annex D.

The additional requirements for circuit-breakers with electronic overcurrent protection are contained in Annex F.

The additional requirements for circuit-breakers for IT systems are contained in Annex H.

The requirements and test methods for electromagnetic compatibility of circuit-breakers are contained in Annex J.

The requirements for circuit-breakers not fulfilling the requirements for overcurrent protection are contained in Annex L.

The requirements for modular residual current devices (without integral current breaking device) are contained in Annex M.

The requirements and test methods for electromagnetic compatibility of circuit-breaker auxiliaries are contained in Annex N.

The requirements for instantaneous trip circuit-breakers are contained in Annex O.

The requirements and test methods for DC circuit-breakers for use in photovoltaic (PV) applications are contained in Annex P.

The requirements and test methods for circuit-breakers incorporating residual current protection with automatic reclosing functions are contained in Annex R.

Supplementary requirements for circuit-breakers used as direct-on-line starters are given in IEC 60947-4-1, applicable to low-voltage contactors and starters.

The requirements for circuit-breakers for overcurrent protection for household and similar installations, and designed for use by uninstructed persons, are contained in IEC 60898 series.

The requirements for circuit-breakers for equipment (for example electrical appliances) are contained in IEC 60934.

For certain specific applications (for example traction, rolling mills, marine service, downstream of variable frequency drives, use in explosive atmospheres), particular or additional requirements can be applicable.

NOTE 1 Circuit-breakers can have dedicated accessories.

NOTE 2 Circuit-breakers which are dealt with in this document can be provided with devices for automatic opening under predetermined conditions other than those of overcurrent and undervoltage as, for example, reversal of power or current. This document does not deal with the verification of operation under such pre-determined conditions.

The object of this document is to state:

a) the characteristics of circuit-breakers;

b) the requirements for circuit-breakers with reference to:

1) operation and behaviour in normal service;

2) operation and behaviour in case of overload, operation and behaviour in case of shortcircuit, including co-ordination in service (selectivity and back-up protection), as well as the operation and behaviour in case of ground-fault;

3) dielectric properties;

4) requirements on electromagnetic compatibility, where applicable;

c) tests intended for confirming that these conditions have been met and the methods to be adopted for these tests;

d) information to be marked on or given with the circuit-breakers.

NOTE 3 For cybersecurity requirements, see IEC TS 63208.

title: Switches for appliances - Part 2-1: Particular requirements for cord switches;
description:
Clause 1 of IEC 61058-1:2016 is applicable except as follows:

Addition:

This document applies to cord switches (mechanical or electronic) for appliances actuated by hand, by foot or by other human activity, to operate or control electrical appliances and other equipment for household or similar purposes with a rated voltage not exceeding 250 V and a rated current not exceeding 16 A.

Throughout this document, the word "appliance" means "appliance or equipment".

These switches are intended to be operated by a person, via an actuating member or by actuating a sensing unit. The actuating member or sensing unit can be integral or arranged separately from the switch. The transmission of a signal between the actuating member or sensing unit and the switch can be made either physically or electrically (for example,  electrical, optical, acoustic or thermal).

Switches which incorporate additional control functions governed by the switch function are within the scope of this document.

This document also covers the indirect actuation of the switch when the operation of the actuating member or sensing unit is provided by a remote control or a part of an appliance such as a door.

NOTE 1 Electronic switches can be combined with mechanical switches giving full disconnection or microdisconnection.

NOTE 2 Electronic switches without a mechanical switch in the supply circuit provide only electronic disconnection. Therefore, the circuit on the load side is always considered to be live.

NOTE 3 For switches used in tropical climates, additional requirements can apply.

NOTE 4 Attention is drawn to the fact that the standards for appliances can contain additional or alternative requirements for switches

title: Controlgear for electric light sources – Safety – Part 1: General requirements
description:
This part of IEC 61347 specifies general safety requirements for controlgear for electric light sources for use on DC supplies up to 1 500 V or AC supplies up to 1 000 V at 50 Hz or 60 Hz.

NOTE 1 In the remainder of this document "light source" is used instead of "electric light source".

This document is only applicable in conjunction with the relevant part(s) of the IEC 61347-2 series.

NOTE 2 As far as covered in the scope of the relevant part of the IEC 61347-2 series, this document is also applicable to controlgear used for electric sources producing optical radiation with the same technology used for purposes different than illumination and producing radiation other than visible spectrum.

title: Controlgear for electric light sources – Safety – Part 2-13: Particular requirements – Electronic controlgear for LED light sources
description:
This part of IEC 61347 specifies safety requirements for electronic controlgear for LED light sources for use on DC supplies up to 1 500 V or on AC supplies up to 1 000 V at 50 Hz or 60 Hz.

This document is applicable for electronic controlgear for LED light sources with an output voltage (RMS) not higher than 1 000 V.

NOTE 1 Control units, such as devices connected between the power supply unit and LED light sources that control or adjust the operation of LED light sources, are covered by this document.

NOTE 2 Performance requirements are covered by IEC 62384.

NOTE 3 Such controlgear can also be used for electric sources producing optical radiation with the same technology used for purposes different than illumination and producing radiation other than visible spectrum.

title: Audio/video, information and communication technology equipment – Part 1: Safety requirements
description:
This part of IEC 62368 is a product safety standard that classifies energy sources, prescribes safeguards against those energy sources, and provides guidance on the application of, and requirements for, those safeguards.

The prescribed safeguards are intended to reduce the likelihood of pain, injury and, in the case of fire, property damage.

The objective of the introduction is to help designers to understand the underlying principles of safety in order to design safe equipment. These principles are informative and not an alternative to the detailed requirements of this document.

title: NORMA Oficial Mexicana de Emergencia NOM-EM-009-ASEA-2026, Distribución de Gas Licuado de Petróleo por medio de Auto-tanque y Vehículo de Reparto
description: The notified Emergency Mexican Official Standard establishes the technical specifications and requirements regarding industrial safety, operational safety and environmental protection that must be met by regulated entities that distribute LPG by road tanker or delivery vehicle.
productsFreeText:
• La Distribución de Gas Licuado de Petróleo por Auto-tanque, a partir del punto de transvase en la planta de distribución o en las instalaciones de almacenamiento para la carga del Recipiente no Desmontable con GLP, el traslado del Auto-tanque y hasta el punto de conexión para la descarga en la Instalación de la Usuaria o Instalación de aprovechamiento de la Usuaria Final, así como las actividades relacionadas con la guarda del Auto-tanque, y
  • La Distribución de Gas Licuado de Petróleo por Vehículo de Reparto, a partir de la recepción de los Recipientes Transportables sujetos a presión y Recipientes Portátiles en la planta de Distribución o Bodega de guarda para Distribución de GLP, el traslado, hasta su entrega en la Instalación de la Usuaria o Instalación de aprovechamiento de la Usuaria Final, así como las actividades relacionadas con la guarda del Vehículo de Reparto.
  • Esta Norma Oficial Mexicana de Emergencia no aplica a los Auto-tanques que carecen de un Sistema de trasiego, destinados al Transporte de Gas Licuado de Petróleo.

       Lo anterior, para el inicio de operación, durante la operación y mantenimiento y hasta el término de la operación de la Unidad de Distribución.

title: Draft Commission Implementing Decision (EU) repealing Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/2279 postponing the expiry date of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for use in biocidal products of product-types 14, 18 and 20 in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council
description:
This draft Commission Implementing Decision repeals the latest postponement of the expiry date of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine as an active substance for use in biocidal products of product-types (PT) 14, 18 and 20.

On 26 February 2020, applications was submitted in accordance with Article 13(1) of the Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council (BPR) for the renewal of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14, 18 and 20. 

Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/1284 postponed the expiry date of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14 and 18 to 31 July 2024. Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/732 postponed further the expiry date of the approval of the substance for PT 14 and 18 to 31 January 2026. Finally, that expiry date was again extended to 31 July 2027 by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/2279. 

In parallel, Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/461 postponed the expiry date of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 20 to 31 January 2026. That expiry date was again extended to 31 July 2027 by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/2279.

On 27 May 2026 the Agency adopted its opinions on aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14, 18 and 20, having regard to the conclusions of the evaluating competent authority.

Given the opinions of the Agency, it is appropriate to renew the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14, 18 and 20. Consequently, a draft Implementing Regulation is being prepared to renew the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14, 18 and 20 (examination procedure under Regulation (EU) No 182/2011).

Further to that Implementing Regulation, it is necessary to repeal the latest postponement of the expiry date of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine. The present draft Decision therefore intends to repeal Decision (EU) 2025/2279 postponing the expiry date of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14, 18 and 20.

descriptionPlain: This draft Commission Implementing Decision repeals the latest postponement of the expiry date of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine as an active substance for use in biocidal products of product-types (PT) 14, 18 and 20.On 26 February 2020, applications was submitted in accordance with Article 13(1) of the Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council (BPR) for the renewal of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14, 18 and 20. Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/1284 postponed the expiry date of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14 and 18 to 31 July 2024. Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/732 postponed further the expiry date of the approval of the substance for PT 14 and 18 to 31 January 2026. Finally, that expiry date was again extended to 31 July 2027 by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/2279. In parallel, Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/461 postponed the expiry date of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 20 to 31 January 2026. That expiry date was again extended to 31 July 2027 by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/2279.On 27 May 2026 the Agency adopted its opinions on aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14, 18 and 20, having regard to the conclusions of the evaluating competent authority.Given the opinions of the Agency, it is appropriate to renew the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14, 18 and 20. Consequently, a draft Implementing Regulation is being prepared to renew the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14, 18 and 20 (examination procedure under Regulation (EU) No 182/2011).Further to that Implementing Regulation, it is necessary to repeal the latest postponement of the expiry date of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine. The present draft Decision therefore intends to repeal Decision (EU) 2025/2279 postponing the expiry date of the approval of aluminium phosphide releasing phosphine for PT 14, 18 and 20.

description:

description: In response to concerns regarding the quality of wooden knock-down furniture and the risks associated with excessive formaldehyde emissions, the Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection (BSMI) proposes to require that wooden knock-down furniture be subject to mandatory inspection before being placed on the market. description:
As required by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC or Commission) announces that the Commission has submitted to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) a request for extension of approval of information collection requirements associated with the Safety Standard for Button Cell or Coin Batteries and Consumer Products Containing Such Batteries. OMB previously approved the collection of information under control number 3041-0195. OMB's approval will expire on 31 October 2026. On 15 June 2026, CPSC published a notice in the Federal Register (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/1964/Add.5) to announce the agency's intention to seek extension of approval of the collection of information. The Commission received three public comments. By publication of this notice, the Commission announces that CPSC has submitted to OMB a request for extension of approval of that collection of information.

 

Submit comments on the collection of information by 4 November 2026. 

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 63275; 5 October 2026:

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF A PRE-EXPORT VERIFICATION OF CONFORMITY PROGRAMME FOR CERTAIN UNREGULATED PRODUCTS IMPORTED FROM THE PEOPLE’S REPUBLIC OF CHINA
description:
The Republic of South Africa wishes to inform WTO Members that, with effect from 22 September 2026, it has withdrawn in its entirety the Ministerial Directive titled “Implementation of a Pre-Export Verification of Conformity Programme for Certain Unregulated Products Imported from the People's Republic of China”, published under Government Notice No. 7284 in Government Gazette No. 54374 of 20 March 2026 and notified to the WTO under G/TBT/N/ZAF/273.

 

Consequently, no Certificate of Conformity is required under the withdrawn Directive, no new applications for Certificates of Conformity will be accepted or processed under the Directive, and any applications pending as of the effective date of the withdrawal will be administratively closed.

 

The withdrawal does not affect obligations imposed under compulsory specifications or any other applicable customs, border-management, consumer-protection, health, safety or sector-specific legislation.

title: Commission Delegated Regulation supplementing and amending Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards minimum values for the electrochemical performance and durability of rechargeable industrial batteries, technical and safety parameters, and standards concerning the battery passport
description:
This draft Commission Delegated Regulation sets limit values for industrial batteries for capacity fade, energy round trip efficiency (residential battery energy storage systems only), and expected lifetime in cycles or years. It contains measurement and calculation methods to help determine whether limit values are met and details whether and how various second life batteries should be evaluated with regard to the limit values.

In addition, the draft amends certain parts of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 in view of technical and scientific progress: the standards relevant for QR codes and unique identifiers for the battery passport and technical parameters concerning performance and durability, safety (stationary battery energy storage systems only) and state of health (stationary battery energy storage systems and batteries for light means of transport).
productsFreeText: Industrial batteries, including residential battery energy storage systems; electric vehicle batteries; batteries for light means of transport (HS code ex 8507)

objectivesFreeText:
Batteries that last longer and display higher performance deliver more energy throughout their useful lifetime. This represents a reduction in their overall environmental impact. Batteries that last longer and perform better are more sustainable. Market competition is currently largely based on price differentiation, without sufficient incentives or rewards for economic operators who produce longer lasting, more performing batteries, with a corresponding lower environmental impact. Therefore, it is necessary to set limit values for the electrochemical performance and durability, as already envisaged under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, in notification G/TBT/N/EU/775; Protection of the environment.

Further, developments in standardisation have resulted in new standards for QR codes and unique identifiers that are of relevance to the battery passport. It has also led to technical and scientific progress on certain technical and safety parameters referred to in Regulation (EU) 2023/1542.

description:
This draft Commission Implementing Decision does not renew the approval of bromoacetic acid for use in biocidal products of product-type 4.

On 22 December 2023, an application was submitted in accordance with Article 13(1) of Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 for the renewal of the approval of bromoacetic acid for use in biocidal products of product-type 4.

On 8 April 2026, the applicant informed the evaluating competent authority that it withdrew their application for the renewal of approval of bromoacetic acid for product-type 4. The draft Decision will therefore propose to not renew the approval of bromoacetic acid for product-type 4.

In order to allow sufficient time for economic operators to adapt, treated articles treated with or incorporating bromoacetic acid for use in biocidal products of product-type 4 may be placed on the market for a period of 180 days after the entry into force of this Decision.

title: Mandatory Application of the Indonesian National Standard for Solid Nitrogen, Phosphor, and Potassium Fertilizer
description:
Regulation of the Minister of Industry of the Republic of Indonesia Number 25 of 2026 concerning Amendment to Regulation of the Minister of Industry Number 11 of 2025 concerning the Mandatory Application of the Indonesian National Standard for Solid Nitrogen, Phosphor, and Potassium Fertilizer mandates product produced nationally or imported, distributed, and marketed in Indonesia shall conform to SNI requirements. All Producers who produce these products shall perform compliance to those requirements, proven by having certificate SNI and SNI Marking product (SPPT - SNI).

The product certificate for SNI marking shall be issued by product certification bodies that have been accredited by KAN and appointed by the Minister of Industry.

Directorate of Upstream Chemical Industry, Ministry of Industry is the responsible institution for the implementation of this decree and shall provide a technical guidance of the decree, which covers procedure of product certification and SNI Marking.

Products which are distributed in domestic market that originated domestically and imported shall meet the requirements consisted in:

  • SNI 2803:2024 NPK compound fertilizer; 

NPK compound fertilizer that was manufactured or imported before this Ministerial Regulation comes into force may continue to be distributed until they reach the end user

title: Mandatory Application of the Indonesian National Standard for Tire
description:
Regulation of the Minister of Industry of the Republic of Indonesia Number 24 of 2026 concerning Amendment to Regulation of the Minister of Industry Number 9 of 2025 concerning the Mandatory Application of the Indonesian National Standard for Tire mandates product produced nationally or imported, distributed, and marketed in Indonesia shall conform to SNI requirements. All Producers who produce these products shall perform compliance to those requirements, proven by having certificate SNI and SNI Marking product (SPPT - SNI).
The product certificate for SNI marking shall be issued by product certification bodies that have been accredited by KAN and appointed by the Minister of Industry.
Directorate of Downstream Chemical and Pharmaceutical Industry, Ministry of Industry is the responsible institution for the implementation of this decree and shall provide a technical guidance of the decree, which covers procedure of product certification and SNI Marking.
Products which are distributed in domestic market that originated domestically and imported shall meet the requirements consisted in:
• SNI 98:2019 passenger car tire; 
• SNI 100:2019 light truck tire; 
• SNI 99:2019 truck and bus tire; 
• SNI 101:2019 motorcycle tire; or
• SNI 6700:2012 motor vehicle inner tube tire.
Tire that was manufactured or imported before this Ministerial Regulation comes into force may continue to be distributed until they reach the end user.

title: Draft Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine "On Amendments to Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 65 of 20 January 2021" (concerning Technical Regulation on cosmetic products)
description:
The draft Resolution provides for an amendment to paragraph 3 of the Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 65 of 20 January 2021 "On Approval of the Technical Regulation on Cosmetic Products" to replace the date "3 August 2026" with "31 July 2027".
The amendment is aimed at eliminating a regulatory inconsistency concerning the transitional period for cosmetic products resulting from the provisions of the Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 976 of 29 July 2026 "On Amendments to Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 65 of 20 January 2021" (notified in document G/TBT/N/UKR/392/Add.1) and the Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 737 of 4 June 2026 "On Amendments to the Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 65 of 20 January 2021" (notified in document G/TBT/N/UKR/351/Rev.1/Add.1).
The draft Resolution therefore replaces the date “3 August 2026” with “31 July 2027” as the deadline for placing on the market cosmetic products that have not been notified and do not comply with the requirements of the Technical Regulation on Cosmetic Products. Such cosmetic products may continue to be made available on the market until 3 August 2030, which remains unchanged.
The draft Resolution does not introduce any new technical requirements for cosmetic products and does not otherwise amend the Technical Regulation on Cosmetic Products.

1. The final text takes into account comments received from industry. title: Draft Decree on the Management of Cosmetics
description:
1. This Decree provides for the management of the production, notification, import, export and circulation of cosmetic products, including:
a) Production and quality control of cosmetic products in Vietnam;
b) Notification of cosmetic products;
c) Management of imported cosmetic products; issuance of Certificates of Free Sale for cosmetic products manufactured in Vietnam;
d) Product Information Files, labeling and advertising of cosmetic products;
đ) Quality management, safety of cosmetic products and cosmetovigilance;
e) Inspection, examination, supervision and post-market surveillance of cosmetic products;
g) Recall of cosmetic products, withdrawal of Management Numbers, and management measures applicable to establishments included in the Key Control List.
2. This draft Decree applies to domestic and foreign organizations and individuals engaged in the production, notification, import, export, circulation and trading of cosmetic products in the territory of Vietnam.

The Draft Decree consists of 10 Chapters and 60 Articles, 
Specifically:
1. Chapter I – General Provisions consists of 06 Articles providing for:
Scope of regulation and subjects of application; interpretation of terms; technical requirements for cosmetic products; risk classification of cosmetic products; implementation of administrative procedures and data management in the electronic environment; and management of the status of Management Numbers.
2. Chapter II – Manufacturing, Raw Materials and Quality Control at Manufacturing Establishments consists of 09 Articles providing for:
- Requirements for cosmetic manufacturing in accordance with Cosmetic Good Manufacturing Practices (CGMP), including requirements for professional personnel;
- Competence, dossiers, processes and procedures for issuance, re-issuance, amendment, temporary suspension, suspension and revocation of Certificates of Eligibility for Cosmetic Manufacturing;
- Decentralization to provincial-level People’s Committees or delegated specialized authorities for the management of Certificates of Eligibility for Cosmetic Manufacturing;
- Inspection of continued compliance with cosmetic manufacturing requirements based on risk groups and risk levels, combining periodic and extraordinary inspections with on-site, remote or data-based assessments;
- Control of the origin, source, quality and legality of raw materials and bulk products used in cosmetic manufacturing.
3. Chapter III – Cosmetic Product Notification consists of 08 Articles providing for:
- Cosmetic products must be notified to the competent state authority before being placed on the market;
- Provisions on dossiers and procedures for cosmetic product notification and post-notification amendments;
- Following notification and disclosure of cosmetic product information, competent state authorities shall conduct post-notification dossier reviews and inspection and surveillance of cosmetic products circulating on the Vietnamese market.
4. Chapter IV – Management of Imported Cosmetic Products and Issuance of Certificates of Free Sale consists of 02 Articles providing for:
Imported cosmetic products must be notified prior to customs clearance, except for cases exempted from notification, such as imports for research or testing purposes, imports by diplomatic missions, or personal gifts not intended for commercial purposes; and provisions on the issuance of Certificates of Free Sale (CFS) for domestically manufactured cosmetic products intended for export.
5. Chapter V – Product Information File (PIF), Labeling and Advertising of Cosmetic Products consists of 05 Articles providing for:
- Cosmetic products placed on the market must have a Product Information File (PIF) in accordance with ASEAN guidelines;
- Requirements for Safety Assessment Reports included in the PIF in accordance with ASEAN guidelines;
- Labeling of cosmetic products shall comply with the laws on goods labeling, while mandatory labeling contents for cosmetic products shall comply with the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive;
- Provisions on electronic labeling, Digital Product Passports and product traceability;
- Advertising of cosmetic products shall comply with the laws on advertising 
6. Chapter VI – State Management of Cosmetic Product Quality consists of 04 Articles providing for:
- Management of the quality and safety of cosmetic products;
- Conditions for circulation of cosmetic products, exemptions from cosmetic product notification procedures, and post-notification management of cosmetic products;
- Quality standards, testing laboratories and validity of test results;
- Cosmetic safety monitoring and cosmetovigilance.
7. Chapter VII – Inspection, Surveillance and Post-Market Control of Cosmetic Products consists of 09 Articles providing for:
- Risk classification and determination of principles, plans and competence for inspection and surveillance of cosmetic products;
- Post-notification dossier review, including review of notification dossiers and documents extracted from the Product Information File (PIF);
- Specialized inspections at cosmetic product notification, manufacturing, importing and trading establishments;
- Sampling, testing and handling of cosmetic products failing to meet quality or safety requirements, and other violations;
- Inspection and surveillance of cosmetic products in the online environment;
- Use of third-party conformity assessment results in inspection activities;
- Costs of sampling and testing, and prices of testing services.
8. Chapter VIII – Recall of Cosmetic Products, Withdrawal of Management Numbers and Risk Management Measures consists of 07 Articles providing for:
- Forms and scope of recall of cosmetic products; procedures for recall; and measures for handling recalled products (remediation, re-export or destruction); - Cases, forms and procedures for withdrawal of Management Numbers; - Risk management measures for establishments on the Key Control List. These establishments are subject to testing before products are placed on the market and to increased inspection. Their issued Management Numbers remain valid, and new notification dossiers continue to be accepted..
9. Chapter IX – Organization of Implementation consists of 06 Articles providing for:
Responsibilities of ministries, sectors, organizations and individuals involved in the manufacture and trading of cosmetic products.
10. Chapter X – Implementation Provisions consists of 04 Articles providing for:
Implementation roadmap, transitional provisions, effective date, and responsibilities for implemenation.

description: The notified draft Amendment to the Mexican Official Standard amends and updates civil protection signs and warnings, in accordance with the criteria for prevention and civil protection applicable to buildings, outdoor areas and/or spaces combining both characteristics, in order to inform the general public of designated places for safeguarding their health and safety, as well as to identify areas that require caution or that are off limits during their time on the premises.G/TBT/N/MEX/585- 2 -

description:

This is a proposed extension of the ICR, which is currently approved through 30 September 2026. This notice allows for an additional 30 days for public comments.

 

Comments may be submitted on or before 30 October  2026.

title: The Safer Affordable Fuel-Efficient (SAFE) Vehicles Rule III for Model Years 2022 to 2031 Passenger Cars and Light Trucks
description:
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), on behalf of the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), is substantially recalibrating the Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) program to bring the program into compliance with the law and to remove previous regulatory distortions which have induced manufacturers to make design decisions that have neither aligned with market demand and the needs of American families nor have delivered the consistent improvements in the fuel economy performance of manufacturer fleets, as Congress intended. This recalibration finalizes amendments to fuel economy standards for light-duty vehicles for model years 2022-2026 and MYs 2027-2031. This final rule also finalizes amendments to compliance aspects of the program, including to vehicle classification and other compliance pathways.

 

This rule is effective 30 November 2026. The incorporation by reference of certain publications listed in the regulations is approved by the Director of the Federal Register as of 30 November 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 61988, 30 September 2026; Title 49 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Parts 523, 531, 533, 536, and 537:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-30/html/2026-19964.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-09-30/pdf/2026-19964.pdf

 

This final rule and previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/2253 are identified by Docket Number NHTSA-2025-0491. The Docket Folder is available on Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/NHTSA-2025-0491/document and provides access to primary and supporting documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number.

title: Draft National technical regulation for fresh rice noodle products (Annex Decree)
description: This draft technical regulation establishes food safety limits and management requirements for fresh rice noodle products, covering: general provisions, technical specifications, sampling and testing methods, management requirements, responsibilities of organizations and individuals, and implementation arrangements.
productsFreeText:
Fresh rice noodle products, comprising: 

- Fresh rice vermicelli and fresh flat rice noodles made mainly from rice or rice flour, with or without fermentation, consumed fresh or after preliminary processing and short-term preservation; 

- Similar products made mainly from rice or rice flour, with high moisture content and short shelf life; fresh hủ tiếu; fresh rice paper sheets; unfilled steamed rice rolls/sheets  excluding dried vermicelli and rice noodle, and instant dried noodle).
